Murugan’s Message to Young Creators at YouTube Impact Summit 2026 Over 18,000 Indian YouTube Channels Have Crossed One Million Subscribers, Reflecting Growing Creator Economy Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi Urging young creators to harness artificial intelligence as a tool for innovation and empowerment, Dr. L. Murugan, Minister of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Dr. L. Murugan Highlights Role of Creator Economy and AI in Building Viksit Bharat at YouTube Impact Summit 2026
Technology May Change Rapidly, But Constitutional Values Must Endure: Dr. L. Murugan’s Message to Young Creators at YouTube Impact Summit 2026
Over 18,000 Indian YouTube Channels Have Crossed One Million Subscribers, Reflecting Growing Creator Economy
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

Urging young creators to harness artificial intelligence as a tool for innovation and empowerment, Dr. L. Murugan, Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, said, “The future should not be: AI versus creators. It should be: AI empowering creators.” Calling upon young creators to “Create with courage. Create with responsibility. Create with purpose,” he emphasised that while “Technology changes rapidly. Constitutional values endure.”

India is not merely a nation of more than a billion people; we are a nation of more than a billion stories, ideas and aspirations.

Delighted to deliver the keynote address at the #YouTubeImpactSummit 2026.

YouTube’s contribution of over ₹18,000 crore to India’s GDP and support… pic.twitter.com/1Ov7DH5uhw

— Dr.L.Murugan (@DrLMurugan) September 29, 2026

Addressing the YouTube Impact Summit 2026, themed “Co-Creating Impact: India’s Digital Leadership and the Orange Economy”, in New Delhi today, the Minister highlighted the growing role of India’s digital and creative economy in driving economic growth, employment and global cultural outreach. The Summit brought together policymakers, technology leaders, creators, entrepreneurs and innovators, with Dr. L. Murugan delivering the keynote address.    

Creator Economy Driving Growth and Employment

According to the YouTube Impact Report unveiled at the Summit, YouTube’s creative ecosystem contributed more than ₹18,000 crore to India’s GDP in 2025 and supported over 9.6 lakh full-time-equivalent jobs across the country.

The Minister noted that content produced in India receives over 15 per cent of its watch time from audiences outside India, while more than 18,000 Indian YouTube channels have crossed one million subscribers.

From Digital India to Creative India

Dr. Murugan highlighted India’s digital transformation through digital payments, digital public infrastructure, startups, artificial intelligence, affordable connectivity and digital education. He emphasised the need to move from consumers to creators, users to innovators and content consumption to intellectual-property creation.

He said digital technology has changed the geography of opportunity, enabling talent from every district, language and community to reach global audiences.

Strengthening the Orange Economy

Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Create in India, Create for the World,” the Minister highlighted the Orange Economy’s three pillars content, creativity and culture.

He said creativity extends beyond entertainment and can generate jobs, businesses, intellectual property, exports and cultural influence.

 

AI to Empower, Not Replace, Creators

Dr. Murugan said AI can assist creators in writing, translation, editing, animation, composition, design and distribution, while human imagination remains central to creativity.

He reiterated that AI should empower creators rather than replace them, while stressing the need for accessible, responsible and ethical use of emerging technologies.

The Summit also featured the unveiling of “Create with AI” films, developed in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT).

 

Government Initiatives for Creative Talent

The Minister highlighted initiatives including WAVES, IICT, Create in India Challenges, Gems of India, WAVES Bazaar, MyWAVES and Creator’s Corner to strengthen pathways for identifying, developing and connecting creative talent with markets.

He also highlighted the Union Budget 2026–27 provision for AVGC content-creator laboratories in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges. He noted that the industry is projected to require nearly 2 million professionals by 2030.

 

Constitutional Values in the Digital Age

Emphasising that “Technology changes rapidly. Constitutional values endure,” Dr. Murugan highlighted the relevance of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity in India’s digital transformation.

Referring to Article 19 and the freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable constitutional restrictions, he stressed that the freedom to create must be accompanied by responsibility.

He also highlighted Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, calling for responsible creation, sharing, verification and innovation in the digital age.

 

Taking India’s Stories to the World

Dr. Murugan emphasised that India’s cultural heritage can reach new audiences through cinema, music, gaming, animation, digital storytelling, design, crafts and literature.

Addressing young creators, he said their language, culture and stories can be global and urged them to create with confidence in India’s diversity.

The Minister said that the future of India’s digital economy will depend on what the country creates with technology, stressing the importance of employment, intellectual property, global opportunities and inclusive growth towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

The Summit highlighted the growing role of India’s digital and creative industries in advancing Viksit Bharat 2047, with the Minister calling for collective efforts to build an inclusive and globally competitive creative ecosystem. Ms. Gunjan Soni, Country Managing Director, YouTube India; Ms. Leslie Miller, Vice President, Global Government Affairs and Public Policy, YouTube; and Shri Senthil Rajan, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, were also present.

******

Mahesh Kuamr/ Aparajita Priyadarshini

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister honours India’s Environmental Champions at 4th Eco Warrior Awards 2026, calls Conservation a National Responsibility
Senior IFS Officer Shri B. K. Singh receives Lifetime Achievement Award; 15 Forest Officers honoured for exemplary contribution to Environmental Conservation
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today presided over the 4th Eco Warrior Awards and Eco Warrior Conclave, organised by the Indian Forest Service Association (IFSA) and Indian Masterminds, in New Delhi. The event brought together senior forest officers, conservationists, policymakers, scientists, civil society representatives and industry representatives to recognise outstanding contributions to forest, wildlife and environmental conservation.

Honoured India’s environmental champions at the 4th Eco Warrior Awards 2026 in New Delhi today.

From beat guards and rangers to frontline forest personnel, they protect our forests, respond to fires and safeguard wildlife habitats—turning conservation policy into action on the… pic.twitter.com/3V1WLhItIg

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) September 29, 2026

Addressing the event, Shri Yadav said India’s forests are vital ecological infrastructure supporting water, climate, soil, biodiversity and livelihoods. He also recognised frontline forest personnel and stressed the role of tribal and forest-dependent communities as conservation partners. The Minister said conservation has become more complex, with forest officers required to manage entire ecological landscapes while balancing development, livelihoods, human aspirations and the needs of wildlife. He said the emerging challenges include climate change, increasingly frequent and unpredictable extreme weather events, forest fires, water stress, habitat fragmentation and invasive species, alongside growing pressure on land and natural resources. He called for a landscape approach that brings together forests, wildlife, agriculture, water, livelihoods and human settlements.

Shri Yadav said conservation is not merely a government responsibility but a national responsibility. He described the Forest Service as a service entrusted with the stewardship of India’s natural capital and acknowledged the contribution of frontline forest personnel, including beat guards, rangers and other staff who patrol forests, respond to forest fires and protect wildlife habitats. He said their contribution must never be forgotten and that they are the people who convert conservation policy into conservation on the ground. The Minister said the Eco Warrior Awards celebrate courage without publicity, service without applause and commitment without immediate rewards, and called for the awards to inspire many more people to work for India’s forests, wildlife and environment. He concluded by saying that India’s conservation journey under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi continues to demonstrate to the world that development and environmental stewardship can advance together.

During the awards ceremony, Shri Yadav presented the Lifetime Achievement Award to Shri Brij Kishore Singh, a 1976-batch IFS officer of the Karnataka cadre, in recognition of his decades-long contribution to forest and wildlife conservation. During his career, Singh played an important role in efforts to combat sandalwood smuggling and the activities of notorious brigand Veerappan, besides contributing to forest protection and wildlife conservation in Karnataka.

Eco Warrior Award Winners

The awards recognised forest officers and conservation professionals across several categories:

Protected Area Management

  • Dr. Prakash Chand Gogineni, Conservator of Forests and In-charge Field Director, Similipal Tiger Reserve, Odisha
  • Shri Manish Singh, DFO, Pilibhit Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh

Recognised for strengthening tiger and wildlife conservation through technology, protection measures and community participation.

Wildlife Protection and Conservation

  • Ms. Selvi S. Senbagapriya, DCF (Genetics), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu
  • Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, DCF, Palampur Forest Division, Himachal Pradesh

Recognised for community-based conservation, scientific monitoring, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, and anti-poaching operations.

Environment Conservation

  • Shri Dharm Singh Meena, Conservator of Forests, Bhagirathi Circle, Uttarakhand
  • Shri Suman Shivashankar Sivachar W.M., DFO, Wokha, Nagaland

Recognised for scientific water conservation and restoration of springs and streams, and for Amur falcon protection, community engagement and conservation of the Doyang Reservoir.

Community Connect

  • Shri Dhawan Kumar Rawat, DFO, Pakke Tiger Reserve, Arunachal Pradesh
  • Shri Gurharsh Singh, DCF, Rampur, Himachal Pradesh

Recognised for linking conservation with community livelihoods and for constructing a timber bridge within six hours following the Samej cloudburst to facilitate rescue operations.

Best Use of Technology

  • Shri N. Jayaraj, Wildlife Warden, Hosur, Tamil Nadu
  • Shri Ramsundar M., Director, Rajgir Zoo Safari, Bihar

Recognised for the use of AI-based surveillance and early-warning systems for elephant protection near a vulnerable railway stretch, as well as digital booking, CCTV surveillance and GPS tracking.

Special Jury Award

  • Ms. Savita Dahiya, DCF, Barmer, Rajasthan
  • Ms. K. Karthikeyani, DFO, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu

Recognised for restoration of Tal Chhapar grassland and improvement of habitat for blackbucks and chinkaras, and for a campaign that removed 239 illegal guns from the landscape while strengthening elephant protection.

Special Projects Recognition

The Special Projects Award recognised Project Elephant and the Great Indian Bustard conservation project in Rajasthan for their significant contributions to species and habitat conservation.

The Eco Warrior Conclave featured three panel discussions focusing on emerging and critical issues in environmental governance and conservation:

  • AI & Technology for Conservation and Natural Resources Management;
  • Role of Corporates in Forest Management;
  • Sustainable Development & Environmental Ethics.

The discussions brought together experts and stakeholders to deliberate on the opportunities and challenges involved in using technology, corporate participation and sustainable development approaches to strengthen conservation outcomes. A photography exhibition showcasing nature photographs captured by civil servants from across India was also organised as part of the event.

The event was attended by eminent personalities from the forestry and conservation sector, including Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi, DG (Forests) and Special Secretary (MoEFCC); Shri Bharat Lal, Former Secretary General NHRC; Ms. Anita Karn, President, IFSA; Ms. Monalisa Dash, General Secretary, IFSA; and representatives of Indian Masterminds, among other distinguished guests.

The Curtain Raiser witnessed participation from representatives of 28 embassies, along with leading aviation stakeholders, underscoring the growing…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Civil Aviation
Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu curtain-raises Routes Asia
23rd Routes Asia to be held from 16-18 March 2027 in New Delhi
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi

Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu today unveiled the Curtain Raiser for Routes Asia 2027 in New Delhi, marking a significant milestone in India's preparations to host the prestigious international aviation event. The Curtain Raiser witnessed participation from representatives of 28 embassies, along with leading aviation stakeholders, underscoring the growing international engagement and collaborative opportunities surrounding Routes Asia 2027.

The 24th edition of Routes Asia will be held from 16–18 March 2027 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, bringing together more than 115 leading airlines, representatives from 55+ countries, airports, tourism authorities and aviation stakeholders from across Asia and beyond.

Minister of Civil Aviation, Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, while unveiling the curtain raiser plaque, presented India's vision for Routes Asia 2027 under the theme “Bharat Aviation Rising: Inclusive Growth – Connecting Asia & Beyond.” He highlighted that guided by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the event comes at an opportune moment as India advances towards becoming the world's third-largest aviation market. He said, “Routes Asia 2027 is coming to the right place, at the right time, with the right opportunity! There is room for more capacity, more airlines and more routes”.

With over 166 airports and plans to develop 100 additional airports over the next decade, India's aviation sector is witnessing rapid expansion. The Minister emphasised the growing importance of the hub-and-spoke model, which can connect more cities and people with emerging markets, creating opportunities for airlines, tourism and economic growth. He also highlighted India's active bilateral aviation engagements, particularly with Southeast Asian countries, and the continued growth in international air travel, with passenger traffic recording a compound annual growth rate of 4.6%.

The Minister extended an invitation to the global aviation community to participate in Routes Asia 2027 and explore India's diverse destinations and expanding aviation opportunities. He underscored the importance of collective stakeholder efforts in connecting Tier-II cities, strengthening international hubs and developing new routes that will shape the next chapter of India's aviation journey.

India formally assumed the hosting responsibilities for Routes Asia 2027 from China West Airport Group during the closing ceremony of Routes Asia 2026 in Xi’an, China, in April 2026, with Airports Authority of India, receiving the hosting baton. The upcoming edition is expected to attract over 2,000 delegates, including decision-makers from leading airlines, airports and tourism authorities.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation, highlighted the transformative role of aviation in connecting people, facilitating trade and creating economic opportunities. Emphasising that international travel should become increasingly accessible and seamless for tourism and business, he underscored the importance of partnerships and route development in strengthening India's aviation ecosystem.

Routes Asia 2027 will provide a strategic platform for strengthening partnerships, developing new air routes and positioning India as a preferred aviation and connectivity destination. The event reinforces India's commitment to inclusive growth, international collaboration and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Divyanshu Kumar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Development of North-East Region
Union Minister  Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Launches  The Trailer of  Documentary Series ‘The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast’
Landmark cultural outreach initiative by MDoNER and NEC to showcase the Culinary traditions, indigenous communities, and economic potential of all eight Northeastern States.
Series adopts a bottom-up storytelling model, placing local food, farmers, and community traditions at the forefront of regional promotion.
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 7:03PM by PIB Delhi

The trailer of documentary series “The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast” was officially launched by Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in New Delhi today . The launch event, was organized by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The event was graced by  MoS MDoNER Dr. Sukanta Majumdar and  attended by senior officials of MDoNER and members of the production team.

The documentary series brings the rich culinary traditions, diverse communities, and vibrant cultural heritage of the eight states of Northeast India into sharp national focus.

Undertaken with the support of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and the North Eastern Council (NEC), the series has been implemented through the North Eastern Region Community Resource Management Society (NERCRMS) and produced by Urban Media Productions in association with Filandering Forker Media. It marks a significant cultural outreach effort by MDoNER to introduce the Northeast to a wider audience through the experiences and authentic stories of the people  of the region.

The documentary series takes viewers on a food-led journey across all eight Northeastern States, exploring the region through its cuisine, communities, and people. The series explores the culinary traditions of the NER rooted in locally available resources, intertwined with interesting facts.

The production of the series involved intraction with local communities and food producers, tracing native ingredients from their origins to kitchens and eventually to the dining table. Through these encounters, the documentary captures not only the food itself, but also the stories, traditions, and people connected to it.

The tariler turns the spotlight on northeastern states , looking at the region  through its food and the people who prepare and share it. Rather than presenting the NER through a single cuisine, the series reflects its diverse communities and distinct geographies, highlighting the localized ingredients, indigenous knowledge, and everyday practices behind a meal, with local voices carrying the narrative.

While food remains at the center of the series, the journey also brings viewers closer to the arts, culture, and landscapes of the Northeast, presenting these elements as part of the broader context in which the region’s culinary traditions have evolved. By placing food at the heart of its storytelling, The Enchanting 8 offers a window into the cultural diversity of Northeast India, connecting viewers with the region through its kitchens, ingredients, and  foodways. The launch marks the beginning of a documentary journey that brings the culinary richness of the Northeast to a wider audience.

PS

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Completes Preparatory Phase for Special Campaign 6
Ministry and its organisations also observe “Swachhata Pakhwada” from 16-30 September
MoPSW goals identifies over 11,000 files and 5,624 e-waste items for disposal
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 29 September 2026: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and its organisations have undertaken extensive preparations for “Special Campaign 6,” the sixth edition of the Government of India's nationwide drive to clean government offices, clear pending work, organise old files and improve institutional efficiency. The preparatory phase of the campaign has run from 15 to 30 September 2026, ahead of the Implementation Phase, which will be carried out from 2 to 31 October, 2026.

Secretary, MoPSW, chaired a review meeting with the Heads of all organisations and Nodal Officers of the Ministry and its organisations to assess preparedness for the campaign. The Secretary emphasised timely action, cleanliness, disposal of pending matters, effective management of e-waste, and proper documentation of activities throughout the campaign.

As part of preparations, MoPSW and its organisations have identified several MP References, References from State Governments, Inter-Ministerial Communications, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO References, Public Grievances and PG Appeals, and Rules/Processes for simplification, along with 185 Cleanliness Campaigns, 6,605 physical files and 4,548 e-files for review and disposal during the campaign. In addition, 5,624 e-waste items have been identified for collection, segregation and disposal in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

MoPSW is coordinating with its organisations through designated Nodal Officers, with progress being reviewed regularly during the Preparatory Phase. The identified activities will now be taken forward in a time-bound manner during the Implementation Phase, from 2 to 31 October 2026, with proper monitoring and documentation of outcomes. An Evaluation Phase, assessing results and best practices from the campaign, is scheduled for 16 to 30 November 2026 under the national framework for Special Campaign 6.

Through Special Campaign 6, MoPSW and all its organisations will undertake concerted efforts towards cleanliness, environmental responsibility, efficient record management, reduction of pendency and responsive governance, with particular focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

MoPSW and its organisations are also observing ‘Swachhata Pakhwada’ from 16 to 30 September, 2026, coinciding with the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 and reinforcing its cleanliness and public participation objectives. Key activities under ‘Swachhata Pakhwada’ include ‘Shramdaan’ and cleanliness drives, cleaning of public places and community institutions, repair and renovation of toilets, awareness and IEC activities, Waste-to-Wealth exhibitions, ‘Swachhata Raths’ and rallies, cleaning of ponds, rivers and beaches, plantation drives, and elimination of single-use plastic.

Clean and well-maintained public spaces play an important role in creating welcoming surroundings for visitors and strengthening…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Textiles Organisations Undertake Cleanliness, Awareness and Environmental Initiatives under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)-

On the occasion of World Tourism Day, the Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) reaffirms its commitment to promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental responsibility under the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026.

Clean and well-maintained public spaces play an important role in creating welcoming surroundings for visitors and strengthening responsible tourism. Through cleanliness drives and awareness activities, JCI encourages public participation, responsible waste management and sustainable practices to keep tourist destinations and public places clean and attractive.

JCI–Bobbili DPC under JCI–Parvathipuram Region undertook a post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness activity under theme of “Sports for Swachhata & Post-Event” Cleanliness at the Old Bobbili Riverbank, Bobbili, as part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026.” The initiative aimed to restore cleanliness and hygiene at the riverbank after the immersion activities and promote responsible waste management and environmental awareness.

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026,” Rampur Bolla DPC under Malda Region, West Bengal, conducted a cleanliness drive at the Maa Bolla Kali Temple, Dakshin Dinajpur, West Bengal, on the occasion of ‘World Tourism Day” on 27th September 2026.

Maa Bolla Kali Temple is one of the prominent religious and tourist destinations in the region, attracting a large number of devotees and visitors. The cleanliness initiative focused on maintaining a clean, hygienic and welcoming environment at the temple premises and its surrounding areas.

The drive aimed to promote Swachhata, environmental responsibility and public awareness, while encouraging collective participation towards proper waste management and the upkeep of religious and tourist destinations. The initiative reaffirmed JCI’s commitment to promoting cleanliness and sustainable practices as an integral part of community life.

Textiles Committee-

The Textile Committee conducted a nationwide Shramdaan drive, "Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath for Swachhata," across its Mumbai Headquarters and Regional Offices premises.

National Jute Board (NJB)-

As part of the observance of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the Officers and Employees of the National Jute Board organised a Book Donation Event at nearby schools, namely Chanchal Kumari Girls High School and Haridas Vidyapeeth.

During the event, students were actively engaged and sensitised about the importance of cleanliness, hygiene and maintaining a clean environment in and around their homes, schools and surrounding areas. The students were encouraged to develop responsible habits and contribute towards keeping their surroundings clean.

Books were also donated to the schools for the benefit of the students. The donated books will be made available through the school libraries, enabling students to read and share them, thereby ensuring that the resources can be accessed by a larger number of students.

The initiative combined the message of Swachhata with the promotion of reading and learning, contributing towards the development of responsible, aware and well-informed students.

National Insitute Of Fashion Technology-

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, NIFT Campuses undertook post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness, with proper collection and segregation of floral waste and offering materials. Flower waste was composted wherever feasible.

Cotton Corporation of India-

The Corporation organized an awareness activity across its offices on 28 September 2026 to promote the importance of Reuse and Recycle as part of responsible waste management. Employees were sensitized about reducing waste by reusing materials wherever possible and ensuring recyclable items are properly collected and recycled. The initiative aimed to encourage sustainable habits, minimize waste generation, and promote the efficient use of resources.

The activity reflects the Corporation’s commitment to environmental stewardship, sustainable practices, resource conservation, and collective action towards a cleaner and greener future.

National Handloom Development Corporation-

राष्‍ट्रीय हथकरघा विकास निगम लिमिटेड, नोएडा -  दिनांक 28 सितम्‍बर 2026 को अपराह्न 2.30 बजे “स्वच्छता ही सेवा” के अंतर्गत निगम के प्रबंध निदेशक महोदय द्वारा “एक पेड़ माँ के नाम” पर रोपित किया गया। इस अवसर पर उन्होंने पर्यावरण संरक्षण एवं हरियाली को बढ़ावा देने के लिए अधिक से अधिक पौधे लगाने तथा उनकी नियमित देखभाल करने का संदेश दिया। “एक पेड़ माँ के नाम” पहल प्रकृति माँ के प्रति सम्मान और हमारी जिम्मेदारी का सुंदर प्रतीक है। यह पौधारोपण न केवल कार्यालय परिसर को हरा-भरा बनाएगा, बल्कि सभी कर्मचारियों को पर्यावरण संरक्षण के प्रति जागरूक और प्रेरित भी करेगा

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Tourism
item.description: Ministry of Tourism India and Italy agree to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism 2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group on Tourism discusses cine-tourism, destination twinning, skilling and B2B engagement Both sides agree to establish focused technical groups and points of contact to advance tourism cooperation Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi The 2 nd India–Italy Joint Working Group (JWG) on Tourism was held on 29 September 2026, co-chaired by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, and Ms. Emanuela Tripi,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tourism
India and Italy agree to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism
2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group on Tourism discusses cine-tourism, destination twinning, skilling and B2B engagement
Both sides agree to establish focused technical groups and points of contact to advance tourism cooperation
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi

The 2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group (JWG) on Tourism was held on 29 September 2026, co-chaired by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, and Ms. Emanuela Tripi, Secretary-General, Ministry of Tourism, Italy.

The meeting brought together representatives from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of External Affairs, Embassy of India in Rome and Indian Association of Tour Operators (IATO) from the Indian side. The Italian delegation included senior officials from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Embassy of Italy in New Delhi and ENIT (Italian National Tourism Board).

The discussions covered a broad range of areas for strengthening tourism cooperation between the two countries, including exchange of tourism data, promotion of lesser-known destinations, cine-tourism, destination twinning, skilling and capacity building, and enhanced Business-to-Business (B2B) engagement.

As a key outcome of the meeting, both sides agreed to establish focused technical groups and designate points of contact to take forward the identified areas of cooperation and facilitate sustained engagement between relevant stakeholders.

The two sides also discussed opportunities for tourism cooperation in the context of the proposed India–Italy Year of Culture and Tourism 2027, with a view to further strengthening cultural and tourism exchanges between the two countries.

The 2nd Joint Working Group meeting reaffirmed the commitment of India and Italy to deepen bilateral cooperation in tourism and create stronger institutional and industry linkages between the two countries.

Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles and Its Organisations Undertake Various Cleanliness and Awareness Activities under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026, an Essay Writing Competition was organised at the Ministry of Textiles on 25 September 2026 on the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat Viksit Bharat.”

 

  • To ensure maximum reach and engagement, activities of the campaign are being shared across social media platforms amplifying the message of cleanliness.

 

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)-

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026,” the Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) undertook various cleanliness and awareness initiatives under the themes of “Sports for Swachhata & Post-Event Cleanliness,” “Clean Public Places,” and “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy.” These initiatives aimed to promote cleanliness, hygiene, environmental responsibility, and active public participation in creating cleaner and healthier surroundings.

The JCI Regional Office–Berhampore conducted a collective cleanliness drive at the Y.M.A. (Young Men’s Association) Sports Ground, Berhampore, Murshidabad district, West Bengal.

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI), Guwahati Regional Office, in association with Uparhali DPC, organized a “Cricket Competition & Sports Ground Cleaning Drive” at Sarpara Playground, Uparhali, Kamrup, Assam. The initiative combined the spirit of sports with the message of cleanliness, encouraging community participation and promoting Swachhata as a Way of Life.

Simultaneously, the JCI Region Office -Siliguri conducted cleanliness drives at the Panjipara Football Ground and the Paschim Magurmari Primary School Playground, Dhupguri, Jalpaiguri, West Bengal.

The initiative focused on promoting cleanliness, hygiene, and environmental responsibility at public sports spaces. JCI officials and participants actively contributed to cleaning the sports ground and surrounding areas, reinforcing the importance of maintaining clean and healthy public spaces.

 

  • JCI organized a Door-to-Door Collection Drive for Used Clothes under the theme “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy. The initiative aimed to encourage community participation, promote the reuse and responsible disposal of used clothes, and create awareness about sustainable waste management practices. The drive highlighted the importance of collective participation in building a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable society.

Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Ltd-

 

Encouraged employees to avoid disposable cups, plates and cutlery and use reusable bottles / cups during meeting and official events.

 

  • CCIC organized Trimming / Pruning of trees in the premises New Delhi.

 

Textiles Committee-

The Textile Committee organized head quarter and regional office a workshop and demonstration session on the theme "Waste to Art" (featuring murals, sculptures, and decorative items) on 24 September 2026.

 HQ MUMBAI

                                               

Regional Office Kanpur                                                           Regional Office Delhi

 

Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts)-

  • Handicrafts organized Sanitation & Hygiene Standards: Deep cleaning and sanitization of washrooms and common facility areas.
  • Floor & Common Area Maintenance: Machine scrubbing, deep cleaning, and polishing of high-traffic corridors and entrance lobbies.
  • Plant & Machinery Area Upkeep: Comprehensive cleaning, dust removal, and water clearance in pump rooms, HVAC areas, electrical panel rooms, and utility zones.
  • Basement & Ramp Sweeping: Cleaning of parking areas, driveways, rooftop, ramps, and stairwells.
  • The activities ensured enhanced operational safety in technical rooms, clean common areas, and high standard sanitation facilities. Continual monitoring will be maintained to sustain these cleanliness standards.

 

 

National Jute Board (NJB)-

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign, the National Jute Board organised a cleanliness drive at Calcutta Jute Mill with the active participation of its officers and employees along with the workers of the jute mill. The cleanliness activities covered the inside and surrounding areas of the mill premises, with a focus on removal and proper disposal of accumulated waste and maintaining a clean and hygienic work environment.

During the programme, the waste management unit and dump yard of the mill were inspected to review the existing arrangements for collection, segregation, storage and disposal of waste. The need for timely disposal of waste and regular monitoring of the dump yard was emphasised to prevent accumulation and maintain cleanliness.

The initiative also promoted awareness among workers regarding cleanliness, responsible waste management and maintaining a litter-free workplace. The joint participation of the National Jute Board and jute mill workers reflected a collective commitment towards cleanliness, environmental responsibility and the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates and lays foundation stone of various projects worth more than ₹1,941 crore to make travel easier for people of Delhi
Shri Amit Shah dedicates Barapullah Elevated Road Phase-3, built at a cost of ₹1,635 crore, to the people of Delhi
Barapullah Elevated Road will provide signal-free connectivity with South Delhi, making travel easier, offering relief from traffic jams, and saving travel time
Shri Amit Shah also lays foundation stone of Modi Mill-Savitri Cinema Flyover and the Loni Underpass
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation stone of various projects worth more than ₹1,941 crore to strengthen connectivity in Delhi and make travel easier for the people of Delhi. He dedicated the Barapullah Elevated Road Phase-3, built at a cost of ₹1,635 crore, to the people of Delhi today.

In a post on X, Shri Amit Shah said, “To strengthen Delhi's connectivity and make travel easier for Delhi residents, today various projects worth more than ₹1,941 crore were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid. The Barapullah Elevated Road Phase-3, built at a cost of ₹1,635 crore, was dedicated to Delhi residents today. This will provide signal-free connectivity between East and South Delhi, making commuting smoother, providing relief from traffic jams, and saving travel time. Additionally, the foundation stones for the Modi Mill-Savitri Cinema Flyover and Loni Underpass were also laid.”

दिल्ली की कनेक्टिविटी को सुदृढ़ और दिल्लीवासियों के सफर को सुगम बनाने के लिए आज ₹1,941 करोड़ से अधिक की विभिन्न परियोजनाओं का उद्घाटन व शिलान्यास किया। ₹1,635 करोड़ की लागत से बना बारापुला एलिवेटेड रोड फेज-3 आज दिल्लीवासियों को समर्पित किया। इससे पूर्वी और दक्षिणी दिल्ली के बीच सिग्नल-फ्री कनेक्टिविटी होगी, जिससे आवागमन सुगम होगा, ट्रैफिक जाम से राहत मिलेगी और यात्रा का समय भी बचेगा। साथ ही, मोदी मिल-सावित्री सिनेमा फ्लाईओवर और लोनी अंडरपास का भी शिलान्यास किया।

— Amit Shah (@AmitShah) September 29, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) Organized Voluntary Blood Donation Camp
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Public Health (Urban) Division of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), in association with the Indian Red Cross Society, successfully organized a Voluntary Blood Donation Camp at its premises at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi today (29.09.2026), reaffirming its commitment to social responsibility and community welfare.

The blood donation camp was inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs. The camp was organized with the dedicated efforts of Shri Ranjit Kumar Tiwary, Additional Director General (Urban Health Services), MoHUA, who lauded the enthusiastic participation of the donors and emphasized that voluntary blood donation is a noble act capable of saving countless lives and he also appreciated the profound spirit of service displayed by the participants. Appreciating the spirit of service displayed by the participants, Hon’ble MoS encouraged everyone to continue supporting such humanitarian initiatives.

 

The Blood Donation Camp received an encouraging response from the officers and staff of the Ministry. Driven by the theme "One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives," a total of 76 officers and staff members voluntarily participated in the blood donation drive, contributing to the overall success of the event.

The Ministry expresses its sincere gratitude to all the voluntary donors, the organizing team and the supporting medical staff from the Indian Red Cross Society for their valuable contribution in making the health and wellness event a success.

"Every Blood Donor is a Hero – Your Donation Can Save Lives."

The…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM Approves Revised GRAP Schedule; Tightens Measures for Vehicles, Dust and Pollution Control
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

The 30th meeting of the Full Commission of the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 28.09.2026, under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, during which the Commission approved modifications to the extant Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) Schedule for the National Capital Region (NCR).

The revised GRAP Schedule includes the following changes:

  • Merging repeated actions on dust measures, MSW management and transport in Stage-I;
  • Moving actions related to DG Sets and entry of Buses (BS-IV & below) from NCR and Adjoining States from Stage-II to Stage-I;
  • Allowing minor relaxation under Action No. 1, Stage-III - including repairing of potholes;
  • Extension of restrictions on plying of BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below- standard LMVs (4-wheelers) to Sonipat in addition to the existing HVD Districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar;
  • Removal of exemption for BS-IV and below goods vehicles (LGVs, MGVs in Stage-III and Trucks/ HGVs in Stage-IV) carrying essential commodities in Stage-III and IV;
  • Restrictions on entry of diesel-operated BS-IV and below-standard LGVs and MGVs registered outside Delhi into Delhi has also been clearly mentioned under Stage- III;
  • Citizens Charter under each stage of GRAP has been modified with additional actions (Do’s and Don’ts);
  • Now, the revised GRAP Schedule has 25 actions in Stage-I, 8 actions in Stage-II, 10 actions in Stage-III and 5 actions in Stage-IV, Total: 48 Actions

 

The Commission also approved an amendment to Direction Nos. 11-18 dated 11.06.2021 for strengthening web portal-based monitoring of dust control measures at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites in NCR. The amendment extends the existing web-portal registration and monitoring mechanism to eligible C&D projects situated beyond municipal limits in urban areas, controlled areas, development areas/ industrial development areas, industrial areas/ zones and highway corridor zones, as applicable under the respective Statutory/ planning frameworks. The existing threshold of plot area equal to or greater than 500 square metres and other requirements under Direction Nos. 11-18 shall remain unchanged.

The Commission took note of Advisory No. 18 issued on 10.09.2026 regarding rescheduling of physical sports competitions scheduled during November-December. The Advisory reiterates that physical sports competitions scheduled in NCR during November-December should be appropriately rescheduled, keeping in view the air quality trends prevailing in the area, particularly in the interest of protecting the health of students.

The Commission took note of the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) for appointment of two full-time Technical Members in CAQM for a period of three years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. Two full-time Technical Members appointed are Shri Mukesh Sharma and Shri Trilok Singh Panwar.

The Commission was apprised of the updated status of Enforcement Task Force (ETF) decisions, inspections, closure and resumption of units. As on 17.09.2026, 1,831 violating units had been issued Closure Orders, out of which 1,479 cases had been considered for resumption post compliance and resumption orders issued accordingly. 126 cases had been transferred to SPCBs/ DPCC for further action where units were found unresponsive, permanently closed or shifted to other locations. During the period from 11.08.2026 to 17.09.2026, the ETF continued to examine cases involving non-compliance and applications for resumption of operations following corrective measures.

The Commission reviewed the progress of greening and plantation activities in Delhi- NCR against the targets fixed for 2026-27. Against the overall target of 4,60,54,740 plantations, covering trees, shrubs and bamboo, 4,13,68,929 plantations have been achieved as on 22.09.2026. Delhi has achieved 62,00,527 against its target of 58,01,386 plantations; Uttar Pradesh (NCR) has achieved 1,85,59,812 against the target of 1,71,44,900 plantations; Rajasthan (NCR) has achieved 1,16,13,092 plantations against the target of 1,07,09,754; while the achievement in Haryana (NCR) stood at 60,00,000 against a target of 1,20,00,000. The Commission emphasised continued follow-up and monitoring by the concerned authorities to achieve the stipulated targets and ensure survival of plantations.

Featuring spiritual artefacts, traditional art, sporting memorabilia and models of major infrastructure…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Uttar Pradesh’s Rich Heritage and Modern Milestones on Display at the Prime Minister Mementos e-Auction 2026
Spiritual landmarks, traditional art, sporting achievements and modern infrastructure come together to showcase the diverse identity of Uttar Pradesh
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

A diverse collection of 99 mementos offers a glimpse into Uttar Pradesh’s cultural heritage, historical legacy and contemporary achievements. Featuring spiritual artefacts, traditional art, sporting memorabilia and models of major infrastructure projects. The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online till October 2, 2026. For details and participation, visit https://pmmementos.gov.in

Among the prominent mementos featured is a detailed model of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, crafted in MDF fibreboard with intricate architectural detailing.

Another memento features the Shri Guru Ravidas Janam Asthan Mandir in Varanasi, highlighting the spiritual and cultural legacy associated with Guru Ravidas.

A framed portrait of Rani Lakshmi Bai depicts the Queen of Jhansi on horseback with her son Damodar Rao, while a contemporary Sanjhi paper-cut artwork from Mathura presents a "Tree of Life with Holy Cows”. The Sanjhi piece also showcases the intricate hand-cutting technique associated with the traditional art form.

Uttar Pradesh’s sporting achievements are represented by a signed shirt belonging to para-athlete Preeti Pal, who won two bronze medals in the 100m and 200m T35 events at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.

The catalogue also features a miniature model of the Meerut Metro, commemorating the inauguration of its 26-km corridor in February 2026.

Other notable entries include a Namo Ghat Varanasi hand namaste memento, a sculptural representation of the distinctive joined hands at Namo Ghat and a Ganga Expressway model featuring Goddess Ganga alongside a miniature representation of the infrastructure project.

Together, these mementos bring different facets of Uttar Pradesh into focus, from its traditions and history to its achievements and landmarks.

item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities”- an initiative under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission (SSM)
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog organised a national workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities” on 28th September 2026, in collaboration with the Golap Borbora State Institute of Panchayat & Rural Development (GBSIPRD), Government of Assam. The workshop focused on strengthening Panchayats as institutions capable of driving inclusive growth, effective public service delivery, and sustainable development at the grassroots, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

The one-day National Workshop was inaugurated by Shri Atul Bora, Minister, Panchayat & Rural Development Department, Government of Assam, as the Chief Guest; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, as the Guest of Honour; Dr. Ravi Kota, Chief Secretary, Government of Assam; and Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development.

The inaugural session highlighted the importance of decentralised governance, spatial planning, capacity development, digitalisation, and convergence for advancing Viksit Gram Panchayats. The deliberations focused on four key areas: decentralised and spatial planning, grassroots capacity development, spatial planning for priority sectors, and integration of spatial planning into the GPDP process.

Participants discussed the constitutional foundation of Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and Part IX of the Constitution. Discussions also focused on clearer activity mapping, adequate financial resources, appropriate staffing, greater decision-making authority, Gram Sabha participation, and institutional accountability. The workshop emphasised the need to move from a sectoral to a spatial and integrated approach to local development. GIS, geospatial data, village master plans, and digital platforms were discussed for identifying local resources, infrastructure gaps, land-use patterns, and development opportunities. Integrating spatial information with GPDP, eGramSwaraj, and Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) was highlighted as a means of strengthening evidence-based and convergence-oriented planning.

Capacity development and institutional strengthening were also central to the deliberations. Participants emphasised equipping elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries with skills in data interpretation, investment prioritisation, resource mobilisation, convergence, and outcome monitoring. Discussions covered devolution, activity mapping, District Planning Committees, digital and hybrid learning, competency development, and last-mile technical handholding. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam (Member, NITI Aayog) called for a shift from sectoral planning to a spatial planning approach, with greater emphasis on human and social capital and the development of local economic clusters.

The workshop identified priorities including clearer functional devolution and activity mapping, improved fiscal resources and own-source revenue mobilisation, stronger capacity and technical support, operational District Planning Committees, and greater convergence across departments and schemes. It also highlighted the need to strengthen the use of spatial and administrative data in GPDPs, Gram Sabha and community participation, and rural-urban planning at the district level.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal ready for Conducting Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi

From October 2 to October 31, 2026, the Ministry of Coal is set to conduct Special Campaign 6 across all administrative offices and PSUs. Aligned with the national "Waste to Wealth" vision, the month-long initiative focuses on scientific e-waste disposal, scrap clearance, office space optimization, and workplace digitalization—fostering sustainable, efficient, and citizen-first governance.

To ensure comprehensive implementation and readiness, key review meetings were conducted:

Ministry-Level Review: Smt. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, chaired a review meeting on September 28, 2026, with Senior Officers across all divisions of the Ministry to establish operational strategy and target benchmarks.

 

PSU & Subordinate Office Engagement: Shri Sanjeev Kumar Kassi, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Coal, chaired a follow-up review meeting on September 29, 2026, with Nodal Officers from Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited (NLCIL), the Coal Controller’s Organisation (CCO), and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPFO).

 

 

Key Highlights and Preparatory Initiatives

Identification & Segregation Drive: The Ministry, alongside its CPSEs, CCO, and CMPFO, is actively identifying obsolete items, physical scrap, and e-waste for systematic review, segregation, and scientific disposal to promote cleaner workplaces and efficient asset management.

Youth Innovation Workshop: Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) organized a "Waste to Wealth Workshop" at WCL Koyla Vihar for the wards of employees. Young participants transformed discarded waste materials into creative prototypes—including spacecraft, robots, cars, and castles—highlighting sustainable practices through youth engagement.

Promoting Cleanliness Awareness: The Coal Controller’s Organisation (CCO) hosted a debate competition on the theme “स्वच्छता और विकसित भारत की परिकल्पना” (Cleanliness and the Vision of a Developed India), fostering active dialogue and environmental awareness among officials.

Through these combined efforts, the Ministry of Coal remains committed to reinforcing robust institutional mechanisms, driving administrative efficiency, and advancing a cleaner, greener India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Safaimitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir  To Be Organised Tomorrow Under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
Shivir To Recognise And Honour Contribution Of Safaimitras And Facilitate Access To Health, Safety And Social Protection Measures
Delhi Chief Minister Smt Rekha Gupta, Union MoSJE Ministers Dr Virendra Kumar And Shri B L Verma To Grace The Occasion
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, will organise the SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir in National Capital here tomorrow.

The Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign being observed from 17 September to 17 October 2026, carries the theme Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat.

The theme of the Shivir is Samman Safai Mitron Ka, Sankalp Swachh Bharat Ka. The Shivir aims to recognise and honour the vital contribution of SafaiMitras and facilitate their access to health, safety and social protection measures.

The Shivir will be organised in hybrid mode. The physical event will be held at Kedarnath Sahni Auditorium, Dr. S.P.M. Civic Centre, New Delhi while Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) and line departments from across the country will participate virtually.

Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon’ble Chief Minister, Government of NCT of Delhi, will be the Chief Guest while Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri Pravesh Wahi, Mayor, MCD, Delhi, will grace the occasion as Guests of Honour.

Shri Sanjeev Khirwar, Commissioner, MCD, Delhi, Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Shri P K Singh, Managing Director, National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), senior officers of the Department and Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment besides other officials will attend the programme.

The SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir will provide a single-window platform for a range of interventions aimed at supporting sanitation workers and their families.

The activities being undertaken by ULBs and RLBs will include preventive health check-ups and screening services for SafaiMitras and their dependents, along with the distribution and demonstration of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits and safety devices.

As part of the programme, a film on the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme will also be screened. The film will highlight the objectives and interventions of the NAMASTE Scheme and underline the importance of ensuring the safety, dignity, welfare and social security of sanitation workers. The screening will further create awareness about the measures being undertaken to promote safe and mechanised sanitation practices and improve the well-being of SafaiMitras.

The Shivir will also focus on facilitating the distribution of NAMASTE ID Cards to validated waste pickers and support eligible sanitation workers and their families in accessing Central and State Government welfare and social protection schemes and services. These include assistance related to housing, tap water connections, sanitation facilities, electricity, LPG, health, life and accident insurance, immunisation, financial inclusion and livelihood support, subject to eligibility.

The welfare schemes and initiatives covered through these interventions include PMAY, AMRUT, Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission, Saubhagya, PM Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat/PM-JAY, PM Suraksha Bima Yojana, PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Mission Indradhanush, Swachhata Udyami Yojana and PM Jan Dhan Yojana, subject to eligibility.

The programme will also feature the felicitation and recognition of SafaiMitras for their vital contribution to public health, cleanliness and community well-being. SafaiMitras will participate in the national event as well as local activities organised across the country.

As part of the programme, the NMBA (Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan) Pledge will also be taken by the participants, reaffirming their collective commitment towards creating a drug-free society and promoting awareness about the harmful effects of substance abuse. The pledge will further reinforce the spirit of social responsibility and encourage individuals and communities to contribute towards the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

The initiative reflects the Government’s continued commitment towards ensuring the safety, welfare and dignity of sanitation workers, while strengthening access to healthcare, safety equipment and social protection. It also reinforces the spirit of collective participation and the vision of Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB signs agreement with Multi Nano Sense Technologies for ₹37.51 crore RDI support to build indigenous multi-gas sensing platform
MEMS-based sensor and AFE SoC to advance from TRL-4 to TRL-9, strengthening India’s capabilities in advanced sensors and semiconductor technologies
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi

From industrial safety and hydrogen infrastructure to energy systems and process monitoring, the ability to detect and accurately measure gases is becoming increasingly important across a wide range of emerging technologies. Giving a boost to indigenous capabilities in this domain, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Multi Nano Sense Technologies Private Limited, Nagpur, Maharashtra for ₹37.51 crore financial support under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The project, with a total approved cost of ₹75.02 crore, focuses on the development of a Platform MEMS + AFE SoC Multi-Gas Sensor, with the objective of taking the technology from TRL-4 to TRL-9. The support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).

Multi Nano Sense is developing an indigenous MEMS TCDIR gas sensor and CMOS AFE SoC platform aimed at enabling reliable and scalable multi-gas sensing in a compact form factor. The technology combines a MEMS-based sensing element with an application-specific front-end system-on-chip for signal acquisition and processing. The platform is designed for applications spanning leak detection, process control and health and safety monitoring, with potential use across industries including refineries, petrochemicals, power, PNG infrastructure, industrial safety, batteries and the hydrogen economy.

The proposed sensor platform is designed around a combination of high sensitivity, low power consumption, miniaturised and intelligent signal processing combination of MEMS Gas Sensor and a custom AFE SoC. The technology is intended to operate across a wide temperature range and in demanding industrial environments, while incorporating features such as auto-calibration, compensation for environmental parameters and software-based gas-library processing. With a targeted response time of less than 200 milliseconds, the platform is being developed for applications requiring rapid detection and monitoring. Its compact architecture, with a sensor package designed to be less than 25 mm × 25 mm × 15 mm, also opens possibilities for battery-operated and embedded applications.

The RDI-supported programme will enable Multi Nano Sense to undertake further development, integration, testing, validation and scale-up of the sensor and AFE SoC platform, with the ultimate objective of taking the technology to TRL-9. The project comes under the Deep Technology sector, with Quantum Technology identified as the sub-sector. While the immediate application is advanced multi-gas sensing, the underlying platform brings together MEMS, semiconductor electronics and intelligent sensing, areas that are increasingly important for building indigenous technology capabilities.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “Sensors are the foundation of many modern technology systems, and indigenous capabilities in sensing and semiconductor technologies are important for both industrial competitiveness and strategic self-reliance. The RDI Fund enables us to support technologies that require sustained development before they can reach widespread commercial deployment. The agreement with Multi Nano Sense demonstrates how such support can help Indian deep-tech companies take advanced sensor technologies from development to scalable, market-ready solutions.”

Representative of Multi Nano Sense Technologies Private Limited said, “The RDI support from TDB will enable us to take our MEMS gas-sensing technology to the next stage of integration, validation and scale-up. Our objective is to develop a compact, low-power and scalable multi-gas sensing platform that can address demanding applications across industries. This support will be instrumental in advancing the technology towards TRL-9 and strengthening indigenous capabilities in MEMS and sensor electronics.”

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Viksit Bharat- G RAM G
“Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)”
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 12:59PM by PIB Delhi

 

A New Framework for Rural Employment and Development

Aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) marks a significant reform in rural development. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 came into force on 1 July 2026 and has been rolled out successfully across all rural areas of the country. The transition from Mahatma Gandhi NREGA to VB-G RAM G has been seamless and disruption-free. Digital systems supporting implementation were operational from the commencement of the new framework.

The Act provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment every financial year. The guarantee covers every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. It promotes empowerment, growth, convergence and saturation for a prosperous and resilient rural Bharat. It focuses on four thematic areas: water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events.

The Act institutionalises a Whole-of-Government approach through convergence-driven and saturation-oriented planning. At its core is the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs). These provide an integrated framework for addressing the diverse developmental needs of Gram Panchayats.

 

Bottom-up Planning Envisaged through VGPPs

Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs) are a key institutional reform under VB-G RAM G. They enable participatory, evidence-based, saturation-oriented, and convergence-driven planning at the grassroots level.

VGPPs put local needs at the centre of rural development planning. They are prepared with the active participation of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat. The Gram Sabha provides due recommendation and approval of the plans. VGPPs enable villages to identify their actual development needs, existing assets and development gaps and prioritise works accordingly.

How the VGPP Process Works

  • Participatory planning: Gram Panchayats identify and prioritise works based on local needs, with the involvement of the Gram Sabha.
  • Asset mapping: The process begins with a comprehensive inventory of existing assets, infrastructure and service delivery gaps within the Gram Panchayat.
  • Coverage of existing assets: The inventory includes assets created under various Central and State Government schemes and programmes.
  • GIS-based planning: The planning process uses GIS, Yuktdhara, PM Gati Shakti, and other digital tools. Geospatial and non-spatial information supports evidence-based and integrated planning based on local needs and existing assets.
  • Gap assessment: Information from these platforms supports spatial planning, better asset mapping, and avoidance of duplication. It also helps identify infrastructure deficits, development priorities, and potential interventions.
  • Convergence across government: VGPPs promote a Whole-of-Government approach by bringing together resources and interventions from different schemes, departments and stakeholders for integrated village development.
  • Multi-level consolidation: VGPPs are consolidated at the Block, District, State and National levels. The consolidated plans contribute to the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack.
  • Permissible works: The VGPP Framework identifies 318 types of permissible works across the four thematic areas.

The VGPP process is intended to support integrated village development through employment-linked asset creation, improved infrastructure and convergence of public interventions.

VB G-RAM G: Progress on the Ground

As of 24 September 2026, VB-G RAM G has recorded significant progress since its implementation on 1 July 2026.

  • Active workers: 10.88 crore in 2026-27
  • Assets created: 2.83 lakh
  • Person-days generated: More than 31.69 crore
  • Women’s participation: 61.65 percent in 2026-27
  • Employment provided to workers on demand:  Over 2.81 crore belonging to about 2.23 crore rural households
  • Works under Execution: 97.17 lakh
  • Approved works readily available to meet future employment demand: 73.24 lakh
  • Active worksites operational: Around 20.16 lakh
  • Number of Gram Panchayats executing works presently across the country: Nearly 2.31 lakh
  • DBT transactions: 3.76 crore in 2026-27
  • Average Wage rate: Rs. 283.24 per day per person
  • Total number of Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards issued: 15.17 crore

Financial Progress

  • A total of Rs.93,841 crore has been allocated to States/UTs as interim allocation for FY 2026-27
  • Out of this, a Mother Sanction of Rs.25,880 crore has been issued as the first instalment to the States/UTs

Technology Enabled Transparency and Governance

Technology is central to VB-G RAM G implementation. Digital systems support worker verification, monitoring, payments, and transparency. They also link employment with sustainable asset creation and rural development.

  • Digital verification: e-KYC and worker attendance are captured through Face Authentication and biometric authentication. It significantly enhances transparency, accountability, and authenticity.
  • Digital work monitoring: Geo-tagging, digital measurement, electronic Measurement Books (e-MB) and mobile-based monitoring support monitoring across different stages of implementation.
  • Digital payments: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) supports payments under the framework.
  • Technology-enabled oversight: Spatial technology-enabled planning, real-time dashboards, and AI-enabled analytics support monitoring, reporting, and corrective action.
  • Digital platforms and capacity building: Dedicated digital platforms, citizen engagement platforms and large-scale capacity building initiatives further support implementation.

Building Rural Development from the Ground Up

VB-G RAM G brings employment, participatory planning and rural development together. Through VGPPs, Gram Panchayats identify local needs, map existing assets and prioritise development works. Technology, convergence and digital systems strengthen implementation, transparency and accountability. The framework links employment with sustainable asset creation, supporting resilient livelihoods and integrated rural development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Two officials apprehended for seeking illegal gratification to facilitate FCRA registration
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi

Acting on specific information received by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Special Cell of Delhi Police, in coordination with central agencies, apprehended two government officials in New Delhi on 28 September 2026. The two officials, one working as a Senior Accountant and the other as an Accountant, had allegedly approached an association and sought illegal gratification in return for facilitating its pending FCRA registration.

One of the officials is presently posted in the Foreigners Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs, while the other, presently posted in a Pay & Accounts Office, had earlier served in the Foreigners Division. Preliminary questioning indicates that they were in contact with certain associations for facilitating their registration and renewal in lieu of illegal gratification. Further investigation is in progress.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has zero tolerance towards corruption, and appropriate legal as well as departmental action is being taken in the matter. All FCRA-related services are delivered online through the FCRA portal, and no intermediary, agent or individual is authorised to facilitate any FCRA service.
