item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Literacy for All
India’s Journey Towards Viksit Bharat
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 11:22AM by PIB Delhi

India’s Literacy Leap: Charting the Path to Full Literacy

Literacy is a foundation of national development. Beyond being an indicator of educational progress, it enables individuals to access opportunities, participate in the economy, and engage meaningfully in society. UNESCO recognises literacy as a fundamental human right and a significant driver of achieving equality, justice, inclusion, and respect for the rule of law. India has made significant strides in improving its literacy rate over the past eight decades. In 1947, the country’s overall literacy rate stood at just 14%, while female literacy was remarkably low at 8%. India has undertaken several initiatives over the years to improve literacy and strengthen its education system. The government introduced the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to reform education at all levels and develop a skilled, adaptable, and future-ready workforce.

 

What is Literacy?

The Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, for the first time defines Literacy as “the ability to read, write, and compute with comprehension, i.e., to identify, understand, interpret and create, along with critical life skills such as digital literacy, financial literacy, etc.” It considers 95% literacy in a State/Union Territory as equivalent to full literacy.

 

In a global context, UNESCO defines Literacy as the ability to read, write, and use numbers, as well as to use digital materials to solve problems in an increasingly technological and information-rich environment-a foundational skill that is central to individuals’ engagement in work, learning, and life. It is an essential component of the right to education and a prerequisite for enjoying other human rights.

 

Measuring Progress in Literacy and Education

India’s literacy rate has made remarkable progress since 1951, increasing from 18.32% in 1951 to 74.04% in 2011. Male literacy rose from 27.15% to 82.14%, while female literacy increased significantly from 8.86% to 65.46%.

The urban literacy rate increased from 34.59% in 1951 to 84.1% in 2011, while the rural literacy rate rose from 12.10% to 67.8%. Between 2001 and 2011, rural female literacy grew by 26%, compared with 10% for rural males, reflecting significant gains in female literacy.

According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025, the literacy rate in urban areas reached 89% for those aged 7 years and above, and 88% for those aged 5 years and above. Among urban residents aged 7 years and above, literacy reached 93.1% for males and 84.8% for females. In rural areas, the literacy rate among those aged 7 years and above was 77.4%, and 76.4% for those aged 5 years and above. Among the rural population aged 7 years and above, the literacy rate was 84.8% for males and 70.3% for females. The overall Literacy rate of the country is 81.1 % as per this survey.

To complement literacy gains, the government has also taken measures to improve school enrolment, retention, and progression. Notable improvements in Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER), transition, and retention rates have been noted since 2014-15. According to the UDISE+ Report (2025-26):

  • School Enrolment: Over 24.72 crore students were enrolled in schools.
  • Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER): Stood at 42.8% at the Foundational stage, 91.7% at the Preparatory stage, 89.6% at the Middle stage, and 71.7% at the Secondary stage.
  • Dropout rates were 1.8% at the Preparatory stage, 3.6% at the Middle stage, and 7.0% at the Secondary stage.
  • Retention rates stood at 98.5% for Foundational, 91.1% for Preparatory, 83.7% for Middle, and 51.9% for Secondary stages.
  • Transition rates improved, with 99.2% progressing from the Foundational to the Preparatory stage, 93.8% from Preparatory to the Middle stage, and 88.3% from Middle to the Secondary stage.

The transition rate refers to the percentage of students who successfully move from one level of education to the next.

Participation in higher education has expanded significantly over the past decade:

  • Enrolment increased from 3.42 crore in 2014-15 to 4.50 crore in 2023-24.
  • GER increased from 23.7% to 30% over the same period.
  • Higher education out-turn increased from 88.28 lakh in 2014-15 to over 1.09 crore in 2023-24.

Higher education out-turn refers to the total number of students who pass out of higher education institutions in a given academic year.

The increase in women’s participation, alongside the inclusion of SC, ST, and other disadvantaged groups, reflects enhanced access and equity. It reflects continued improvement in access to higher education, supporting NEP 2020’s target of attaining a 50% higher education GER by 2035.

Key Government Initiatives for Advancing Literacy

India’s approach to literacy has evolved from basic reading and numeracy to broader competencies needed to participate in a rapidly changing economy and society. In line with NEP 2020, the Government has introduced initiatives such as ULLAS and NIPUN Bharat to expand access, strengthen learning outcomes, promote inclusion, and support lifelong learning.

ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) 

ULLAS - Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram: ULLAS, or the New India Literacy Programme (NILP), is a centrally sponsored initiative. It aligns with NEP 2020. It focuses on empowering adults aged 15 years and above who missed formal schooling. The programme provides functional literacy, numeracy, critical life skills, and lifelong learning opportunities. This promotes the social integration of the target group and encourages their contribution to national development.

ULLAS’s vision is ‘Jan Jan Saakshar’, empowering every individual through literacy. It follows the spirit of ‘Kartavya Bodh’ (Duty). It promotes volunteerism and Janbhagidari, or community participation, to achieve universal literacy.

ULLAS follows a hybrid learning approach. The ULLAS App, available on iOS and Android platforms, has teaching-learning material in 27 languages. Under the scheme, learners and volunteers are identified by surveyors at the district- or block-level. They may include school teachers, civil society workers, ASHA workers, and Anganwadi workers. Surveyors conduct door-to-door surveys to identify non-literate individuals and potential volunteer teachers. In the next stage, learners are connected with a Voluntary Teacher to support and guide the students in registering on the ULLAS App.  Training, orientations, and workshops are conducted through face-to-face and online modes. Learners access learning materials and develop foundational literacy and numeracy skills. They then appear for the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test (FLNAT), followed by evaluation and certification.

ULLAS’s Progress and Impact: The scheme aims to cover 5 crore learners during 2022-27 with a financial outlay of ₹1,037.90 crore. ULLAS has about 4.03 crore registered learners and over 52.20 lakh volunteers. To date, more than 3.3 crore learners have participated in the FLNAT.

Ten (10) States/UTs have declared themselves fully literate between 2024 and 2026. These include Ladakh, Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Sikkim, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir. ULLAS is expanding adult literacy through community participation, reaching millions of learners while advancing India’s goal of universal literacy.

NIPUN Bharat: (National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy)

Launched in July 2021, under the aegis of Samagra Shiksha, the initiative focuses on strengthening early learning and supporting continued academic development. It seeks to achieve universal foundational literacy and numeracy by 2026-27, ensuring that every child acquires foundational skills by Grade 2. The mission focuses on the Foundational Stage of ages 3 to 8 years.

In addition, the Government has undertaken several initiatives to increase enrolment and improve retention in schools. Key initiatives include Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI (Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India), PM e-VIDYA, and PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman).

  • Samagra Shiksha focuses on enhancing school effectiveness and ensuring equal opportunities for schooling to improve learning outcomes. The scheme is aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG-4) on education. It was introduced by subsuming the three erstwhile schemes-Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE). The scheme promotes equitable, inclusive, and quality education, with a focus on foundational learning, teacher development, and vocational integration.
  • Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) seeks to strengthen more than 14,500 exemplar schools across the country. The scheme focuses on the holistic and well-rounded development of students by fostering an equitable, inclusive, and joyful learning environment that addresses diverse backgrounds, multilingual needs, and varied academic abilities.
  • PM e-VIDYA is a comprehensive initiative that brings together various efforts related to digital, online, and on-air education to provide multi-mode access to learning. The initiative is expected to benefit nearly 25 crore school-going children across the country.
  • PM POSHAN is a centrally sponsored scheme that provides one hot cooked meal to 11.20 crore students enrolled in Bal Vatikas and Classes I to VIII across 10.36 lakh government and government-aided schools on all school days. The scheme aims to provide nutritional support and encourage greater school participation among students.

Together, these initiatives create an enabling environment that enhances enrolment, retention, and learning outcomes. They also address literacy across age groups and learning stages, strengthening foundational education, adult literacy, and lifelong learning.

Literacy for Viksit Bharat and Sustainable Development

The SDGs provide a comprehensive framework for promoting a more equitable, inclusive, and sustainable future for all. Literacy and education are central to SDG 4, which seeks to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for all. Literacy is positively associated with GDP and per capita income and contributes to economic growth and national development. For India, achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat requires a literate, educated, and skilled population.

Beyond education, literacy contributes to women’s empowerment, equality, inclusion, and the realisation of human rights, while enhancing employability, productivity, innovation, and economic participation. Education and skills can also enable participation in green jobs, support the circular economy, and contribute to environmental sustainability. Thus, progress in literacy can create multiplier effects across the SDGs, supporting inclusive, sustainable, and broad-based development.

Looking Ahead: Advancing Literacy for All

India’s literacy journey since Independence reflects a wider transformation in nation-building and human development. Literacy today extends beyond reading and writing. It enables learning, livelihoods, empowerment, and meaningful participation in society. Initiatives such as NEP 2020, ULLAS, and NIPUN Bharat are broadening this vision. They connect foundational learning with adult education, lifelong learning, and future-ready skills. Aligned with SDG 4, these efforts reinforce India’s commitment to inclusive and equitable development.

As India moves towards Viksit Bharat, sustained implementation remains essential. Greater attention to regional and gender disparities will help ensure that the benefits of literacy reach every section of society. A literate, skilled, and empowered population can become a strong foundation for a more inclusive, productive, and sustainable Viksit Bharat.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister hands over India’s first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme to Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation and a Bamboo Farmer from Odisha
PRAMAAN a vital instrument to meet emerging Global Requirements for Responsible Deforestation-free Timber Sourcing and Livelihood Generation: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 11:16AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today handed over the first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), in New Delhi. The event was organised by the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal, as the scheme's operating agency. Senior officers of the MoEFCC along with senior officers of various States Forest Departments, representatives of certification bodies and industry  attended the event.

PRAMAN certificates were presented to the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC) for its plantations over an area of 33,000 hectares, and to Shri Govind Mohapatra, a farmer associated with Odisha Bamboo Development Agency (OBDA). The plantations underwent a rigorous field and management audit before certification. The certificates mark the culmination of the processes established since launch of IFWCS by the Ministry in December 2023, signifying its transition from a policy framework to field-level implementation across both forest plantations and tree-based farming.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav described PRAMAAN as a vital instrument for Indian producers, exporters and forest-based enterprises to meet emerging global regulatory requirements, including due-diligence and responsible deforestation-free timber sourcing norms adopted by major international markets. As global trade increasingly links market access to verifiable sustainability credentials, he said, PRAMAAN positions India not merely to comply, but to lead in the sustainable forest management and tree outside forest management systems, under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Vocal for Local and Act Global’. He expressed happiness that several State Forest Departments, Forest Development Corporations, farmers and industries have applied for Forest Management, Tree Outside forest Management and Chain of Custody certification and the same are in various stages of process.

The Minister highlighted that PRAMAAN’s accreditation architecture, benchmarked against international certification frameworks, ensures that certification issued under the scheme carries recognition from both domestic and global buyers and regulators. He noted that the PRAMAAN’s forest management certification is anchored in the principles of the National Working Plan Code (NWPC) 2023 ensuring that certification is built on a foundation of forest management audited by third-party rather than voluntary self-declaration alone. 

Emphasising that PRAMAAN is as much a livelihood mission as a trade instrument, the Minister said that by bringing rural and tribal communities, small holder farmers, and forest-dependent communities into a structured and verifiable certification system, the certification scheme opens new income pathways to compliant and premium markets without adding to the compliance burden on producers. He added that women Self Help Groups and marginal landholders engaged in NTFP collection and processing, farm and agroforestry and any tree-based agriculture system stand to benefit.

Placing the initiative with a wider national vision, Shri Yadav stated that PRAMAAN reflects India’s broader journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. It signifies a developed India that combines economic growth with ecological stewardship and that is recognized globally not just as a producer of sustainable goods but a leader in sustainable governance. The Minister complimented IIFM and the ministry, and concluded by calling upon the certification bodies, state forest departments, tree growers, farmer producer organisations, farmer producer companies, Industries, institutions, to strengthen their participation in PRAMAAN so that India’s forests, and the communities who depend on them are positioned at the centre of the next generation of global sustainable trade.

About PRAMAAN

PRAMAAN (Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of sustainable Management practices for Agroforestry And Natural forestry resources) is a nationally accepted, credible, and transparent framework for certification of forests, wood and non-timber forest products with the mission to promote linkages to domestic and international markets for certified forests and agroforestry products. The IFWCS-PRAMAAN certificate enhances the social, and ecological values of India’s forests, agroforestry systems and the Indian wood-based industries. 

The Forest Management certification is assessed against the Indian Forest Management Standard, which are part of the National Working Plan Code 2023.  The core principle of certificate rests on independent audit by certification bodies accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) under the Quality Council of India, rather than on self-declaration alone. PRAMAAN’s accreditation architecture is benchmarked against international frameworks, ensuring recognition among domestic and global buyers and regulators.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the six qualities that invite success
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 8:48AM by PIB Delhi


The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting six qualities-diligence, courage, patience, capacity for action, knowledge and valour. He emphasised that when these qualities are present in a person, even divine assistance is said to come to their aid.

The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam-

“उद्यमः साहसं धैर्यं बुद्धिः शक्तिः पराक्रमः।

षडेते यत्र वर्तन्ते तत्र दैवं सहायकृत्॥”

The Subhashitam conveys that for the person who possesses these six qualities - diligence, courage, patience, the capacity for action, knowledge and valor - even God himself is present to offer assistance.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

“उद्यमः साहसं धैर्यं बुद्धिः शक्तिः पराक्रमः।

षडेते यत्र वर्तन्ते तत्र दैवं सहायकृत्॥”

उद्यमः साहसं धैर्यं बुद्धिः शक्तिः पराक्रमः। षडेते यत्र वर्तन्ते तत्र दैवं सहायकृत्॥ https://t.co/LTBPxDbYtG

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) September 29, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Ho'nble Union Minister for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh launched Live Stock insurance portal
The digital platform aimed at transforming livestock insurance delivery across the country under the Livestock Insurance activity of National Livestock Mission (NLM)
Ho'nble Union MoS for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Prof S P Singh Baghel was also present on the occasion
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 9:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, today launched the Livestock Insurance Portal (https://rashtriyapashubima.dahd.gov.in), a comprehensive digital platform aimed at transforming livestock insurance delivery across the country under the Livestock Insurance activity of National Livestock Mission (NLM).

The Portal was launched by Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, in presence of Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, Animal Husbandry and Dairyingand other senior officials of the Department, representatives of State Governments, insurance companies and sectoral stakeholders. Besides, more than 4,000 participants joined online.

While highlighting the contours of scheme, premium rates, contribution of the farmer & other aspects of scheme on the Livestock Insurance activity, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary (AHD) informed that more than 30 lakh animals have already been insured during the year.

Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying expressed concern over uncertainty of agriculture and expressed hope that the livestock insurance portal will be a great relief to the farmers.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, highlighted that livestock serves as a critical source of income and livelihood for millions of rural households. He emphasized that timely and affordable insurance protection safeguards farmers against financial losses arising from mortality, disease outbreaks, accidents, natural calamities and other unforeseen risks. He stressed upon the measures for awareness programmes for the farmers, to provide them maximum benefit under the scheme. He also urged the Insurance Companies, State Governments and other stakeholders to give wider publicity to the scheme through their respective social media and IEC campaigns.

The newly launched Livestock Insurance Portal provides an end-to-end digital ecosystem for policy issuance, premium management, claim processing, beneficiary verification and real-time monitoring. The platform brings together farmers, State Governments, Insurance Companies and implementing agencies on a single transparent and technology-enabled interface.

The Portal is expected to:

  • simplify and expedite livestock insurance enrolment
  • enhance transparency and accountability in claim settlement
  • enable real-time tracking and monitoring of policies
  • improve accessibility and ease of doing business for farmers and insurance providers
  • strengthen data-driven decision-making for effective scheme implementation.

The initiative marks a significant step towards digital transformation in the livestock sector and supports the Government's vision of leveraging technology for farmer welfare and rural prosperity.

The program follows the successful completion of its first cohort, which comprised more than 40…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Rashtriya Raksha University to Launch Second Batch of Masters in Financial and Economic Security
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 8:44PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai, 28 September 2026

 

Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, with the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, is set to launch the second batch of its Masters in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) program in November 2026. The program follows the successful completion of its first cohort, which comprised more than 40 professionals from diverse fields, including banking, law enforcement, investigation, academia, entrepreneurship and legal services.

Designed especially for working professionals, the one-year program is offered in a hybrid mode, enabling participants to continue their professional responsibilities while gaining specialised knowledge and practical skills. The program places strong emphasis on practical learning, hands-on training and exposure to contemporary challenges in financial and economic security.

 

Building Capacity for Emerging Financial and Economic Threats

Financial security and economic integrity are increasingly important in an interconnected global economy. The rapid evolution of financial technologies, digital assets and cross-border financial activities has also created new avenues for financial crime and economic disruption. There is therefore a growing need to build a specialised cadre of professionals capable of understanding, preventing and responding to emerging financial and economic crimes, thereby strengthening India’s economic resilience and contributing to international peace, stability and security.

 

Speaking at the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Mumbai, Mr. Sunil Kavishwar, Director, School of Criminal Law and Military Law, RRU highlighted the growing importance of safeguarding the integrity and resilience of financial systems. He noted that financial crimes are continuously evolving, moving beyond traditional forms into emerging areas such as virtual digital assets, terror financing, proliferation financing, and technology-enabled financial crimes. The increasing use of sophisticated technologies by criminal networks has further created new challenges for enforcement, regulatory and financial institutions.

Mr. Kavishwar highlighted that RRU has taken the lead in developing a global platform for capacity building, specialised training and knowledge exchange in the emerging field of financial and economic security. The University is working towards bringing together professionals, experts and institutions from across relevant domains to strengthen specialised understanding and practical capabilities in this area. He further highlighted that the MFES program brings together not only academicians but also experienced practitioners and working professionals who bring direct expertise from the field and will contribute to the program as faculty and resource persons.

Mr. Harshit Singh, Teaching Cum Research Officer, RRU spoke about the importance of developing a specialised professional cadre equipped to address emerging financial and economic security challenges. He emphasised that such trained professionals can contribute to strengthening India’s economic resilience, supporting sustainable national growth and enhancing the country’s contribution to global financial security and stability.

The program also aligns with the broader vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Viksit Bharat @2047, by contributing to the development of skilled professionals capable of protecting financial systems, strengthening institutional capacity and responding effectively to emerging economic and security threats. As India’s economy becomes increasingly integrated with global financial systems, such specialised expertise can play an important role in supporting secure, resilient and sustainable growth.

The second cohort is open to national and international participants, providing an opportunity for professionals from different jurisdictions and sectors to learn and engage with contemporary issues of financial and economic security. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is also a Knowledge Partner in the program.

Interested professionals can register through the official Rashtriya Raksha University admission portal. The program is intended to provide participants with a multidisciplinary understanding of financial and economic security through academic instruction, practical exposure and interaction with experts from the field.

For further information and registration, visit the official Rashtriya Raksha University website.

 

* * *

item.category: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India showcases Forest and Landscape Restoration Initiatives at COFO 28, in Rome
International Cooperation must support Country-driven Implementation, Capacity Development, Technology Transfer and Measurable Outcomes on Ground: India
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 8:21PM by PIB Delhi

India highlighted its significant achievement in forest and landscape restoration and reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable forest management, climate action and resilient forest landscapes at the Twenty-eighth Session of the FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) Committee on Forestry (COFO 28), being held in Rome from 28th September to 2nd October 2026. Delivering its Statement during COFO 28, India welcomed FAO’s focus on Forest and Landscape Restoration, and emphasised that sustainable forest management provides an integrated framework for addressing restoration at the landscape level while responding to national circumstances and the needs of local communities.

India highlighted the consistent progress made in enhancing its forest resources. The country’s forest and tree cover stands at 82.74 million hectares, constituting 25.17% of its geographical area. The FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 ranks India 9th globally in forest area and 3rd in net annual forest area gain. Forests and trees also remain central to India’s climate commitments. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.29 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2021 and has enhanced its ambition to create an additional carbon sink of 3.5–4.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2035, compared with 2005 levels.

The Statement further highlighted its commitment under the Bonn Challenge to restore 26 million hectares of degraded and deforested land by 2030, of which 21.76 million hectares have already been brought under restoration. Further, major landscape restoration initiatives being undertaken were showcased. Under the Aravalli Green Wall, approximately 6.45 million hectares of degraded land have been identified for restoration. In coastal landscapes, the MISHTI initiative is advancing mangrove restoration while strengthening climate resilience and supporting local livelihoods. India also highlighted that the number of Ramsar Sites in the country has reached 101.

The country also showcased Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam – Plant4Mother, a whole-of-government and whole-of-society initiative under which more than 3.5 billion saplings have been planted. India emphasised that international cooperation must move beyond global commitments to support country-driven implementation, capacity development, technology transfer and measurable outcomes on the ground. It underlined the need for effective and sustainable financing, particularly for developing countries, and encouraged FAO to strengthen support for accessing climate, biodiversity and blended finance and for developing long-term restoration programmes.

India also called for stronger coherence between FAO’s forestry work, the Global Forest Goals and other forest-related international processes, along with enhanced South-South and triangular cooperation for sharing knowledge, best practices and scalable solutions. The country reaffirmed its commitment to working with FAO and Member States in shaping the proposed UN Decade for Afforestation and Reforestation in line with Sustainable Forest Management, 2027–2036, with the objective of building a coherent continuum from restoration of degraded ecosystems to resilient, productive and inclusive forest landscapes.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
DoWR, RD & GR to implement Special Campaign 6 during 02-31 October, 2026
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 8:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Water Resources, RD & GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti, has initiated preparations for Special Campaign 6, which will be implemented across the Department & its organisations from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, in line with the Guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign will focus on institutionalizing cleanliness practices, improving space management and ensuring timely disposal of pending VIP/PMO etc. references in Government offices.

On 28.09.2026, Smt Archana Varma, Secretary, DoWR, RD & GR chaired a meeting with the Heads of Wings/Organisations of the Department regarding the preparatory phase of Special Campaign- 6. During the meeting, the preparedness of the Department and its organisations with regard to various activities/parameters under the campaign was reviewed. Secretary, DoWR instructed the officials to finalise the targets and to make all efforts to meet the targets by the end of Special Campaign- 6.

 

This year Campaign will accord special emphasis to scientific management of ewaste, with focus on effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures. This will contribute towards environmentally responsible office management and sustainable workplace practices.

With Special Campaign 6, DoWR, RD &GR reaffirms its commitment in making cleanliness an integral part of daily office practices and ensuring the timely resolution of public matters in the spirit of transparency, efficiency and citizen-centric governance.

Further, Building on the achievements of the previous Special Campaign, DoWR, RD & GR has continued its efforts towards reducing pendency and ensuring timely disposal of various categories of references and public matters. The progress has been regularly monitored and updated on the SCDPM Portal of DARPG.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
India Energy Week 2027 Sets the Stage for Global Energy Dialogue in Kolkata
Hon’ble Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri alongwith Hon’ble Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari formally announce Kolkata as the host city for India Energy Week 2027
Kolkata to host India Energy Week 2027
IEW 2027 theme: “Unlocking Innovation. Securing Energy. Shaping Tomorrow.”
75,000+ energy professionals and 700+ international exhibitors expected
IEW 2027 will be held from 28–31 January 2027 at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata, India
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

As India’s energy demand continues to grow amid a rapidly shifting global energy landscape, the technologies, partnerships and strategic choices shaping the future of energy will be at the forefront of India Energy Week (IEW) 2027.

Making its debut in Kolkata from 28–31 January 2027 under the theme “Unlocking Innovation. Securing Energy. Shaping Tomorrow,” the fifth edition of IEW will serve as the first major global energy conclave of the year, bringing together policymakers, energy leaders, technology innovators, investors and industry stakeholders from across the world to explore pathways to strengthen global energy security and advance sustainability.

Held under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India Energy Week has grown rapidly since its debut in Bengaluru in 2023, expanding in scale, international participation and the breadth of issues addressed. At the fourth edition in Goa in 2026, the event brought together 75,000+ energy professionals, 700+ exhibiting companies, participants from more than 120 countries and 6,500+ conference delegates, reflecting its preeminent position among global energy conclaves.

Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri along with Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari formally announced Kolkata as the host city for India Energy Week 2027. Shri Adhikari thanked Shri Puri and the Petroleum & Natural Gas Ministry for bringing IEW 2027 to West Bengal. Shri Adhikari said a successful IEW 2027 would help attract new investment, expand existing projects and create employment opportunities in West Bengal.

The evolution of India Energy Week has taken place alongside India’s increasing importance to the global energy system. As the world’s fastest-growing major economy, India’s energy demand is expanding rapidly, while the country continues to balance energy security and affordability with its transition towards cleaner energy systems. India’s energy choices therefore have implications well beyond its borders, making the country a centre of the global energy conversation.

IEW 2027 will build on this context, focusing on the technologies, innovations and partnerships required to ensure energy security, affordability and sustainability for the globe, especially countries in the global South. The event will provide a meaningful platform for stakeholders from across the hydrocarbon and wider energy value chain to explore opportunities to scale innovation, strengthen energy security, improve efficiency and accelerate technology-led progress.

With energy security, affordability, technology, investment and sustainability increasingly interconnected, IEW 2027 promises to catalyse global efforts to find practical solutions to the challenges shaping the sector. The exhibition and conference programmes will showcase developments across oil and gas, LNG, refining and petrochemicals, hydrogen, biofuels, digitalisation and AI, alongside other emerging areas within the energy sector.

Kolkata: A New Chapter for India Energy Week

The move to Kolkata brings India Energy Week to eastern India for the first time, adding a new geographical dimension by providing a platform for businesses, institutions and energy stakeholders from the region to engage with international partners and participate in global conversations on energy.

The fifth edition is expected to bring together 75,000+ energy professionals and 700+ international exhibitors, alongside the decision-makers in the energy domain. The exhibition and conference programmes will provide opportunities to showcase technologies, forge partnerships and explore the strategic opportunities and challenges shaping the energy sector.

The international character of India Energy Week has also grown alongside its scale. Previous editions have brought together senior government leaders and energy executives from major energy-producing and consuming economies. 17 Ministers and Deputy Ministers from countries including UAE, Canada, Netherlands, Oman, Brunei, Myanmar, Tanzania participated in IEW 2026, along with International organisations such as the International Energy Forum, BIMSTEC and the Eurasian Economic Union.

Their participation reflected the increasingly interconnected nature of the energy conversation, as countries and companies navigate questions around energy security, investment, technology, transition and the changing global energy landscape.

About India Energy Week

India Energy Week is the country’s flagship global energy platform, bringing together government leaders, industry executives and innovators to accelerate progress toward a secure, sustainable and affordable energy future. As a neutral platform, India Energy Week drives investment, policy alignment and technological collaboration shaping the global energy landscape.

Held under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India Energy Week 2027 is being organised by Federation of Indian Petroleum Industry (FIPI) with Informa Markets as Conference Organiser.

India Energy Week 2027 will take place from 28–31 January 2027 at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata, under the theme “Unlocking Innovation, Securing Energy, Shaping Tomorrow.”

For more information, visit: https://www.indiaenergyweek.com/

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Union Minister of Education Shri Pralhad Joshi holds bilateral meeting with H.E. Mr. Philippe Baptiste, Minister of Higher Education, Research and Space of France, in New Delhi
Hon’ble Ministers discuss academic mobility, institutional linkages, research collaboration, innovation and emerging areas of cooperation
French Minister H.E. Mr Philippe Baptiste is on a three-day visit to India from September 28 to 30, 2026
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Philippe Baptiste, Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space of France, in New Delhi today. The two Ministers discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation between India and France in education, research, innovation, academic mobility and institutional partnerships.

Welcoming the French Minister and his delegation, Shri Pralhad Joshi highlighted the longstanding India-France partnership and emphasised that cooperation in education is an important pillar of the bilateral relationship. He said that the India-France Year of Innovation 2026 provides a timely opportunity to further deepen collaboration in education, research and innovation.

The Minister also thanked the Government of France for its support in hosting the inaugural edition of Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice, France. The Bharat Innovates platform provided Indian deep-tech start-ups with an opportunity to showcase their innovations before a global audience and facilitated greater engagement between India and France in education, research, innovation and emerging technologies.

During the meeting, the two sides deliberated on the potential engagements in the field of higher education including strengthening institutional linkages, mobility of students, faculty and researchers, and expanding opportunities for collaborative academic programmes and exchanges. The also explored greater cooperation in life sciences, social sciences and humanities, with emphasis on institutional interaction, collaborative academic activities and research.

The Ministers exchanged views on further promoting research, innovation and knowledge partnerships between the two countries and discussed opportunities to build upon existing institutional collaborations and create new avenues for joint academic and research initiatives. French Higher Educational Institutions were invited to explore opening of branch campuses in India including in GIFT City, Gujarat and also at places where French companies are located and require technical human resources.

Acknowledging the importance of people to people ties, the two sides explored opportunities to strengthen language learning and teacher education, share academic expertise and promote technology-enabled learning. The discussions also covered ongoing revision of the Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ) Agreement between India and France, sharing experiences and best practices in digital education and leveraging technology to expand access to quality learning.

The meeting concluded with both sides reaffirming their commitment to further deepen India-France cooperation in education, higher education, research, innovation, academic mobility, language education and digital learning.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ in New Delhi
The Conference deliberated upon the seven pillars of PRAHAAR including Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts and Recovery & Resilience through a whole-of-society approach
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has adopted a 'zero-tolerance' policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism
Consistent efforts are required to strengthen the 'PRAHAAR' strategy through a continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishing a strong and concrete 'PRAHAAR' mechanism for the next 10 years
Union Home Minister impressed upon adopting a proactive approach towards every aspect of the 'PRAHAAR' initiative to ensure its implementation down to the police station level
There is a need to institutionalize an automated counter-terrorism response at every level of the 'PRAHAAR' framework
Better coordination among all stakeholders is essential to prevent any delays in action and to ensure that every pillar of 'PRAHAAR' is result-oriented
Union Home Minister launched a new Extradition Portal, which will synergise and expedite the efforts to bring back fugitives from abroad
From 2019 to 2026, the Modi Govt. successfully brought back 288 fugitive criminals to India from 36 countries
As a result of better coordination among agencies, more than 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics were busted, more than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals were arrested across 15 states
At the same time, Modi Govt. declared Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under UAPA
State police forces should establish dedicated teams to work intandem withcentral agencies to bring back fugitives from abroad
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ today in New Delhi. The Conference deliberated upon the seven pillars of PRAHAAR including Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts and Recovery &Resilience through a whole-of-society approach. The Conference was attended by Union Home Secretary, Foreign Secretary, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs, DGsP of 15 States, ATS Chiefs of all the States/UTs in person while other State DGsP and cutting-edge police officers joined the Conference virtually.

In his address, Union Home Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has adopted a 'zero-tolerance' policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism.He also stressed on the need for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise the PRAHAAR strategy through a continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishing a strong and concrete PRAHAAR mechanism for the next 10 years. Focussing on percolation of the tenets of PRAHAAR up to the Thana level, he impressed upon adopting a proactive approach towards every aspect of the PRAHAAR initiative. Mentioning various steps undertaken for mitigating terrorist threats, he advocated institutionalising an automated counter terrorism response at every level of the framework. Impressing upon the necessity of result-oriented approach towards each pillar of PRAHAAR, he called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action. Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said, from 2019 to 2026, the Modi Govt. successfully brought back 288 fugitive criminals to India from 36 countries.  As a result of better coordination among agencies, more than 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics were busted, more than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals were arrested across 15 states. He said, at the same time, Modi Govt. declared Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under UAPA.

Union Home Minister also launched a new Extradition Portal, which will synergise and expedite the efforts to bring back fugitives from abroad. He exhorted the State Police Forces to establish dedicated teams for working in tandem with the Central agencies to bring back fugitives from abroad.

Nadda Reviews Progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College and its Associated Hospitals Shri Nadda Emphasises Long-Term Vision, Quality and Timely Execution for Upcoming Infrastructural Projects Union Health Minister visits Advanced Simulation-Based Training and Neonatal Care Facilities at LHMC and KSCH; Highlights the role of simulation-based training and advanced neonatal care in strengthening patient safety and clinical outcomes Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Health…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College and its Associated Hospitals
Shri Nadda Emphasises Long-Term Vision, Quality and Timely Execution for Upcoming Infrastructural Projects
Union Health Minister visits Advanced Simulation-Based Training and Neonatal Care Facilities at LHMC and KSCH; Highlights the role of simulation-based training and advanced neonatal care in strengthening patient safety and clinical outcomes
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda reviewed the progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC) and its associated hospitals, Smt. Sucheta Kriplani Hospital (SSKH) and Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital (KSCH), with a focus on strengthening healthcare infrastructure, specialised clinical services, medical education, research and patient care.

During the review meeting, the Minister was apprised of the ongoing augmentation of Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital. The project envisages increasing the hospital’s total bed capacity from 394 to 894 beds, ICU capacity from 40 to 200 beds and the number of Operation Theatres from 4 to 12. Construction work on the KSCH campus is underway and is aimed at strengthening tertiary and super-speciality paediatric care, while also expanding capacity for undergraduate, postgraduate and super-speciality medical education and training.

Addressing the review meeting, Shri Nadda emphasised that the ongoing and upcoming projects at LHMC and its associated hospitals must be planned with a patient-centric and future-oriented approach, keeping evolving medical requirements at the core. He stressed that planning and design should draw upon the expertise and best practices of leading institutions in the relevant fields, while ensuring high quality of construction and strict monitoring of project timelines. He called for timely escalation of issues requiring approvals and clearances to the Ministry and emphasised that infrastructure expansion and recruitment of nurses, doctors and other healthcare professionals must progress concurrently.

Looking ahead, he called for a comprehensive master plan with a long-term institutional vision, combining immediate priorities with phased development and a forward-looking perspective for the coming decades. He also encouraged exploring private-sector expertise and partnerships, wherever appropriate, in planning and implementing major projects, while ensuring that quality, efficiency and patient care remain central to all such initiatives.

As part of the visit, the Union Health Minister visited the state-of-the-art Skill Lab at Lady Hardinge Medical College, a comprehensive multidisciplinary simulation-based training facility that provides hands-on and competency-based learning in a safe and controlled environment. The facility has dedicated simulation areas for ICU, surgical skills, simulated OT, Obstetrics OT, NICU, trauma, ENT and ophthalmology, along with briefing and debriefing areas and task trainers for procedural skills.

The Skill Lab provides an integrated platform for undergraduate and postgraduate training, procedural skills development, faculty development, multidisciplinary team training and competency-based assessment. Simulation-based learning, deliberate practice and structured feedback at the facility support the development of clinical and surgical proficiency, decision-making, teamwork, communication and crisis-resource management, while contributing to enhanced patient safety.

The Minister also visited the recently functional Augmented Level III-B Neonatal Care Centre at Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital and reviewed the advanced facilities available for newborn care.

The Department of Neonatology has 80 intensive care beds and caters to more than 10,000 deliveries and 2,500 NICU admissions annually, with overall survival exceeding 93 per cent. The neonatal care facility provides advanced services including high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV), inhaled nitric oxide therapy, therapeutic hypothermia, advanced monitoring and comprehensive respiratory support.

The recently functional NICU-B comprises 7 NICU beds, 8 HDU beds, 15 Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) beds and 12 mothers’ cots, with emphasis on family-integrated care, kangaroo mother care and breastfeeding support.

The review and visit underscored the continued efforts of LHMC and its associated hospitals to strengthen advanced patient care, specialised paediatric and neonatal services, medical education, simulation-based training and research, alongside the ongoing expansion and modernisation of healthcare infrastructure.

Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, National Health Authority (NHA); Dr. L.G. Krishna, DGHS; Smt. G.S. Chitra, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family welfare and Dr. Himani Ahluwalia, Director, Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC); Dr. Arvind Kumar, Medical Superintendent, LHMC; Dr. Vikram Dutta, Medical Superintendent, LHMC and Dr. Sujata Gautam, Principal, LHMC were present at the review meeting.

The Shram Samvad Campaign, launched with effect from today, is aimed at creating awareness among stakeholders regarding the recently introduced Labour Codes and the key provisions and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
District Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad as part of Shram Samvad Initiative
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour and Employment organised a District Awareness Programme, as part of its “Shram Samvad” Awareness Campaign, at the Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad today. The Shram Samvad Campaign, launched with effect from today, is aimed at creating awareness among stakeholders regarding the recently introduced Labour Codes and the key provisions and compliances applicable thereunder. Industrial clusters across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories will be covered over the next 90 days under this initiative.

The programme at Faridabad witnessed enthusiastic participation from around 75 participants including employers, state authorities, advocates and other representatives and stakeholders from the labour and employment ecosystem. It was structured into five informative sessions, covering the major provisions of the new Labour Codes, employer compliances, and key social security schemes of the Government of India.

The inaugural address was given by Ms. Mridula Ghai, ACC, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), and Ms. Aprajita Jaggi, ACC, EPFO. Mr. Ashish Wig, Member, Central Board of Trustees & Chair HR and IR Committee, PHDCCI, also addressed the gathering on this occasion.

The first technical session was conducted by Mr. Minhaz Ahmed, Director, Ministry of Labour and Employment. He provided an overview of the new Labour Codes, explaining their objectives and highlighting the major provisions and changes introduced under the new legislative framework. The session focused on providing participants with a broad understanding of the Labour Codes and their significance for employees and employers.

The second session was conducted by Mr. Hemant Tirkey, Labour Welfare Commissioner, who elaborated upon the major compliances to be undertaken by employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical insights into the responsibilities and statutory requirements applicable to employers and helped participants understand the compliance framework under the new Codes.

The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Mr. Sunil Gautam, Assistant Welfare Commissioner. The participants were apprised of the salient features of the scheme and its role in extending social security benefits to eligible unorganised workers.

The fourth session was dedicated to the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was conducted by Mr. Pranit Joshi, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I. The session provided participants with an overview of the scheme, its objectives and the relevant provisions and benefits associated with it.

The programme concluded with an interactive Question and Answer session, wherein participants actively engaged with the speakers and raised queries relating to the implementation and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes. The session provided an opportunity for participants to seek clarifications on various aspects of the Codes and related labour welfare schemes.

The programme served as an important platform for awareness generation and stakeholder engagement, facilitating a better understanding of the new Labour Codes, employer compliances and Government initiatives aimed at strengthening labour welfare and social security.

*****

Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Department of Food and Public Distribution Continues Swachhata Hi Seva-2026 Campaign with Cleanliness Drives and Public Awareness Activities
DFPD Promotes Cleanliness, Hygiene and Community Participation through Swachhata Hi Seva-2026
DFPD Organises Door-to-Door Awareness Campaign, Walkathon and Plogging Drive to Promote Cleanliness
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Government of India, including all its PSUs, attached/ subordinate offices are conducting activities under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva-2026’ campaign as per guidelines of Department of Urban Development and Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation for the cleanliness and sanitation.

The DFPD organized a door-to-door awareness campaign at Firoz Gandhi Camp, New Delhi on 21.09.2026. The officials of the department visited the camp and distributed brooms, dustbins, soaps, sanitizers to the residents of the camp. The officers briefed the residents about the importance of not only keeping their houses but also their surroundings clean. The children of the residents were also sensitized about personal hygiene and keeping their environment clean.

The DFPD organized a spirited Walkathon & Plogging Drive from Krishi Bhawan to Jantar Mantar on 22.09. 2026.The event inspired citizens to embrace cleanliness and reaffirmed commitment to a Swachh Bharat.

Swachhata Samvad, a cleanliness dialogue program was also organized in the DFPD on 23rd September 2026. On this occasion, officials of the department actively participated, shared ideas, and further strengthened the resolve for cleanliness. In the program Smt. Abha Kumar, Sr. Vice President, Sulabh International Social Service Organization, shared her views on the importance of cleanliness.

On the occasion of Swachhata Hi Seva-2025, the officials of the Department visited market area nearby Krishi Bhawan on 24.09.2025 to promote Swachhata awareness and advocate for clean public spaces. The market area was cleaned, and dustbins were distributed to street vendors to encourage proper waste disposal and maintain cleanliness.

The Department also organized a Health check-up camp at Krishi Bhawan on 24.09.2026 in association with MASSH Super Specialty Hospital, New Delhi with their team of Senior Doctors including lab technicians. In the camp, various tests like blood sugar, Blood pressure etc. for Safai Mitras/Security Guards and Officials were conducted to ensure their well-being.

A Poem recitation competition on the theme "Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” was organized on 25.09.2026 in which the officials of DFPD participated.

Meanwhile the following activities have also been undertaken by the PSUs and Attached offices of the Department: -

On 22.09.2026, officers and employees of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) Headquarters and RO Maharashtra, RO Odisha, RO Haryana, organized a Swachhata Rally as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign. During the rally, participants actively engaged in cleanliness activities in the surrounding areas, markets and other public places along the route.

Cleanliness drive at public places such as hospitals, schools, roads etc. on 22.09.2026 by QCCs.

Awareness programmes for employees and young staff were organized on 23.09.2026 across all FCI offices, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, Divisional Offices, and Depots. These activities included Essay Writing Competitions, Poster-Making and Wall-Painting Competitions, Quizzes, and Slogan-Writing Competitions focused on cleanliness and sanitation. The activities encouraged collective efforts towards realizing the vision of a clean, hygienic, and sustainable India.

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign, Food Corporation of India (FCI) Headquarters and its subordinate offices, including Regional Offices, Divisional Offices and Depots, organised on 24.09.2026, awareness camps and outreach activities at nearby Government Schools and Anganwadi Centres across the country. The initiatives focused on nurturing the values of cleanliness, hygiene, sanitation and responsible waste-management practices among children.

IGMRI Ludhiana organised a “Neki Ki Deewar” on 24.09.2026 for the collection and reuse of usable clothes, promoting cleanliness, reuse and community welfare under “Swachhata Hi Seva-2026”. 

Through these initiatives, the Department of Food and Public Distribution and its associated organisations continue to encourage active participation among employees, citizens and communities in promoting cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene and responsible waste management, contributing towards the vision of a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

 

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit the United States to Participate in G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting
Shri Goyal to Engage With Leaders of American Industry, Investors and The Startup Community in Milwaukee, Chicago and New York
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will visit the United States of America from 29 September to 5 October 2026. Shri Goyal will participate in the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting to be held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 30 September and 1 October 2026, at the invitation of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR).

The Meeting will bring together Trade Ministers of G20 members. India will engage constructively with all G20 members and work towards a rules-based, open, inclusive, transparent, equitable and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organization at its core, while ensuring adequate policy space for developing countries. On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal will hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts. The engagements will focus on expanding opportunities for farmers, fishermen, women entrepreneurs, startups, MSMEs and other enterprises.

Shri Piyush Goyal will also engage bilaterally with his counterpart from the United States as part of ongoing efforts to advance a balanced and mutually beneficial India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and finalise an interim deal in line with the Joint Statement of 7 February 2026.

In Milwaukee and Chicago, Shri Goyal will meet chief executives of leading American companies in manufacturing, consumer goods, agri-business, retail and technology, and participate in roundtables with businesses, startups and innovative companies. He will highlight the opportunities India offers as a manufacturing and investment destination and invite American companies to deepen their partnerships with Indian enterprises.

In Chicago, Shri Goyal will pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi on Gandhi Jayanti and Swami Vivekananda. He will also interact with professional associations representing the Indian community.

The visit is expected to further strengthen the trade and investment partnership between India and the United States and deepen India’s engagement with its G20 partners.

 

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Tamil Nadu’s Cultural Heritage and Sporting Achievements Featured in PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
The collection spans sacred traditions, classical art, traditional craftsmanship, historic figures and sporting memorabilia from across the state
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

Tamil Nadu is represented by 31 mementos in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, showcasing the state’s spiritual traditions, art, craftsmanship, historical legacy and sporting achievements.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online till October 2, 2026. For details and participation, visit https://pmmementos.gov.in

Notable mementos from Tamil Nadu include:

Among the notable mementos is an Auspicious Framed Footprint from Kanyakumari, presented by the Vivekananda Rock Memorial. The piece is associated with Sri Padhaparai, which is traditionally believed to bear the footprints of Goddess Kumari

A memento of Sant Shri Ramanujacharya Ji features an intricately detailed depiction of the philosopher and theologian in a teaching pose, reflecting his spiritual and intellectual legacy.

The collection also includes a Thiruvalluvar Chariot, a handcrafted model inspired by the traditional temple chariots of Tamil Nadu.

 

The sporting memorabilia includes a badminton racket associated with para-badminton player Nithya Sre Sivan, who won a medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, and a signed racket of Thulasimathi Murugesan, who won silver in badminton singles at the Paralympics.

 

The collection also features shoes associated with Mariyappan Thangavelu, a three-time Paralympic medallist in high jump.

 

Tamil Nadu’s devotional and artistic traditions are represented by a metallic Nataraja statue, depicting Lord Shiva in his cosmic dance.

 

A Tanjore-style Veena artwork, embellished with gold foil and Kundan stones, is another notable piece.

Other prominent entries include a traditional Tanjore painting of Lord Murugan, a gold-foil depiction of Lord Murugan, a framed devotional work featuring Sri Sowmya Narayana Perumal, and a brass presentation memento depicting the Madurai Meenakshi Amman Temple. Traditional textiles are also represented by South Indian angavastras featuring zari and woven borders.

The 31 mementos together offer a glimpse into Tamil Nadu’s diverse cultural landscape, bringing its spiritual traditions, classical art, craftsmanship, historical figures, textiles and sporting achievements to the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026.

***

M Annadurai

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Second India-Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group Meeting Held in New Delhi
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:11PM by PIB Delhi

The second India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group (JWG) meeting was held in New Delhi on September 28, 2026.The two countries held discussions on a wide range of areas of mutual interest, including military training and capacity building, service-to-service engagements, maritime security, cyber training, defence industry collaboration and enhanced institutional cooperation between the Armed Forces of India and Fiji.

India reiterated the importance accorded to Fiji and the Pacific Island Countries in its vision of a free, open, inclusive and secure Indo-Pacific. Both sides expressed satisfaction at the growing bilateral defence engagements and reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cooperation in mutually beneficial areas. 

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Amitabh Prasad, Joint Secretary (International Cooperation), Ministry of Defence and Mr. Mason Smith, Permanent Secretary for Defence & Veterans Affairs, Fiji. Mr. Smith also met Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh on the sidelines of the 2nd India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group Meeting. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral defence and maritime cooperation, including opportunities for greater defence industry collaboration.

As part of efforts to expand specialised military training cooperation, the Fijian delegation is scheduled to visit Kochi on 29–30 September 2026. The delegation will inspect facilities at the Southern Naval Command to formalise advanced naval training cooperation and professional aviation training modules, enhancing technical proficiency and operational synergy between the two maritime forces.

Prior to the commencement of the official bilateral talks, Mr. Smith paid solemn tribute to India's fallen soldiers at the National War Memorial, New Delhi. The Fijian delegation also visited the DPSU Bhavan at the World Trade Centre, New Delhi, where it was briefed on India's indigenous defence manufacturing capabilities. The visit highlighted advancements under the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' initiative, with a focus on exhibition displays and advanced Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality (AR/VR) simulation facilities that replicate real-world battlefield conditions.

India and Fiji share close and friendly relations, underpinned by historical, cultural and people-to-people ties. The meeting provided an opportunity to consolidate the existing defence partnership and identify new avenues for cooperation. Both sides agreed to maintain regular engagements and work towards further deepening bilateral defence cooperation.

The initiative is aimed at strengthening safety standards, practices, accident prevention and safety awareness across the steel industry. The Council will be headed by the Secretary, Ministry of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Steel
Ministry of Steel Announces Apex Body for  Strengthening Safety Standards and improve safety culture in Steel sector
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Steel, Government of India, has decided to set up a Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) as an apex-level industry safety body under the administrative control of the Ministry of Steel. The initiative is aimed at strengthening safety standards, practices, accident prevention and safety awareness across the steel industry.

The Council will be headed by the Secretary, Ministry of Steel, as Chairman and will include senior officials of the Ministry, Chief Executives of integrated steel producers, and representatives of key technical and statutory organisations including the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS), Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and recognised steel technology institutions.

The SISC will assess the safety situation in the steel industry, facilitate studies and improvements in safety practices, approve industry safety standards and recommended practices, and review serious accidents, accidents and near-miss incidents. It will also provide directions for strengthening safety awareness, training and preventive measures.

To provide technical and professional support to the Council, a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (SISD) will be established. The Directorate will have expertise in areas including process safety, blast furnaces, steel melting, rolling mills, coke ovens, refractory systems, electrical and mechanical safety, occupational health, fire engineering and disaster management.

The SISD will oversee implementation of the Council's decisions, undertake periodic safety audits and reviews, maintain and disseminate accident and near-miss information, conduct investigations into serious safety incidents, review emergency preparedness and safety training programmes, and develop and issue Steel Industry Safety Standards, Recommended Practices and Guidelines suited to Indian conditions.

The establishment of SISC and SISD represents an important institutional step towards promoting a stronger safety culture, improving prevention of industrial accidents and advancing consistent safety practices across India's steel industry.

***

Both sides agreed to expand and deepen defence cooperation activities through exchange of personnel from training institutes, exploring avenues for joint…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Second JDC meeting between India and Ethiopia held in Addis Ababa
Posted On: 28 SEP 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

The second Joint Defence Cooperation meeting between India and Ethiopia was held today, September 28, 2026, in Addis Ababa. The two countries discussed areas of mutual interest in the fields of military training, military exercise, medical cooperation, peacekeeping and defence industries. Both sides agreed to expand and deepen defence cooperation activities through exchange of personnel from training institutes, exploring avenues for joint ventures in defence production, delegation visits and experience sharing interactions.

This visit marks a pivotal step in India-Ethiopia defence relations and reinforces both side’s commitment to work together. It is also part of the institutional mechanism set up through signing of the Defence Cooperation MoU in February 2025 by the Defence Ministers of both the countries. The 1st JDC was held in New Delhi in October 2025. 

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Sanjay Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Defence and Major General Teshome Gemechu, Director General for Defence Foreign Relations & Military Cooperation, Ethiopia. The Indian delegation comprised officers from the Department of Defence and Air Headquarters. Shri Devesh Uttam, Ambassador of India to Ethiopia, also participated in the meeting. 

Ethiopia is an important defence partner of India and the partnership started way back in 1958. During the visit of Prime Minister of India to Ethiopia in December 2025, the bilateral relationship between the two countries was elevated to the level of ‘Strategic Partnership’. 

 ***

SR/NJ
