item.title: The Ministry of Minority Affairs strengthens its infrastructure, entrepreneurship and monitoring drive through partnerships with strategic institutions at IISc Bangalore on September 25, 2026
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Minority Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Minority Affairs The Ministry of Minority Affairs strengthens its infrastructure, entrepreneurship and monitoring drive through partnerships with strategic institutions at IISc Bangalore on September 25, 2026 Collaborations with CUBE, IIT Madras, IISc-FSID, IIM Bangalore and IIMB Innovations to strengthen quality assessment, independent monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation and economic opportunities for minority communities Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, entered into a number of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
The Ministry of Minority Affairs strengthens its infrastructure, entrepreneurship and monitoring drive through partnerships with strategic institutions at IISc Bangalore on September 25, 2026
Collaborations with CUBE, IIT Madras, IISc-FSID, IIM Bangalore and IIMB Innovations to strengthen quality assessment, independent monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation and economic opportunities for minority communities
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, entered into a number of Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with prominent academic, research and innovation institutions at IISc Bengaluru on 25 September 2026, in the presence of Dr. Srivatsa Krishna, Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs and other senior officials of the Ministry and institutions. Through these, the Ministry has made significant strides in strengthening the implementation and impact of key initiatives of the Ministry, with a focus on infrastructure quality, independent monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation, skilling and sustainable economic opportunities for minority communities.

The collaborations bring together the institutional strengths of the Centre for Urbanization, Buildings & Environment (CUBE), IIT Madras; Foundation for Science Innovation and Development (FSID), IISc Bengaluru; Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore); and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL).

These partnerships will enable the Ministry to access specialised technical and academic expertise, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, improve monitoring and assessment mechanisms, support innovation and entrepreneurship, and create stronger institutional pathways for capacity building and enterprise development.

Independent third-party monitoring of PM VIKAS training

In a bid to strengthen transparency and accountability under the Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) Scheme, the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, and Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) signed an agreement for independent third-party monitoring of PM VIKAS training across the South zone.

Under this partnership, IIMB will conduct field-level inspections and concurrent monitoring, assessing training delivery, infrastructure, beneficiary and trainer participation, attendance, certification and placement outcomes through on-ground verification and stakeholder consultations.

The evidence-based insights generated through the partnership will help the Ministry strengthen implementation quality, identify and address gaps, improve monitoring mechanisms and enhance outcomes under PM VIKAS.

Independent third-party assessment of PMJVK infrastructure projects

The Ministry of Minority Affairs signed an MoU with CUBE, IIT Madras, for independent third-party quality (technical & social) assessment of infrastructure projects under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK).

The assessment will cover selected completed and ongoing PMJVK projects across the sectors of education, health, skill development, and women & child development. It will focus on key parameters, including infrastructure quality, functionality, accessibility, utilisation, maintenance and sustainability.

 

This partnership will provide the Ministry with independent, evidence-based assessments and actionable recommendations, enabling better asset management, identification of implementation gaps and more informed planning for future PMJVK projects. It will also deepen the understanding of the functionality and utilisation of infrastructure assets and contribute to more sustainable outcomes.

Strengthening entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystems

The two tripartite MoUs signed by the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) with the Foundation for Science Innovation and Development (FSID), promoted by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL), the entrepreneurship and incubation centre of the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, will establish a framework of cooperation to strengthen the startup and innovation ecosystem and promote economic growth of minority communities.

The collaboration with FSID, IISc Bengaluru focuses on startup ecosystem development, innovation promotion and technology commercialisation, along with data governance, digital transformation and public interest technology.

The MoU with IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL) focuses on strengthening the startup ecosystem, along with skilling and capacity building, innovation and entrepreneurship promotion, research studies, policy support and evidence-based decision-making.

Under the Prime Minister Minority Venture Fund (PM-MVF) framework, these collaborations envisage entrepreneurship awareness and capacity-building programmes, innovation challenges and startup identification, incubation and mentoring, investor connect, market access and enterprise development. They also provide access to knowledge networks, institutional support, industry linkages and innovation ecosystems, with a focus on developing scalable, sustainable and innovationdriven enterprises.

The two collaborations bring together the complementary strengths of IISc-FSID in deep-science and deep-technology incubation, technology commercialisation and innovation promotion, and IIMB-NSRCEL in entrepreneurship, incubation, marketoriented opportunities and fintech. Together, they seek to support minority entrepreneurs and strengthen their access to startup and innovation ecosystems.

A collaborative approach to inclusive development

The signing of these MoUs represents a collaborative approach towards strengthening the impact of initiatives of the Ministry by bringing together technical expertise, academic knowledge, research capabilities and established entrepreneurship ecosystems.

While addressing the gathering, Dr. Srivatsa Krishna said, “The focus of the government is EEE to enable employment through entrepreneurship. The focus of the MoUs with premier technology institutions in the country, namely:

- Indian Institute of Science Bangalore

- Indian Institute of Management Bangalore

 - CUBE of Indian Institute of Technology Madras

is to synergise and bring together their expertise to make this mission possible. 

The end goal is to select, curate and fund those startups which can create employment through entrepreneurship and ensure that the quality of built assets for the minority community and their utilisation is at par with the best. "

Speaking on the occasion, Professor U Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIM Bangalore, said, “IIMB values the responsibility entrusted to it through such efforts, particularly where its expertise can help strengthen public programmes and their outcomes. Through our Centres of Excellence, both of which have over 25 years of experience in creating impact on the ground, we are keen to bring our understanding, knowledge and capabilities to initiatives that can expand opportunities for minority communities as well as enable pathways for enterprise.”

While the partnership with CUBE, IIT Madras strengthens independent assessment and evidence-based improvement of PMJVK infrastructure, the collaborations with IIM Bangalore, IISc-FSID and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL) create institutional pathways for entrepreneurship, innovation, incubation, skilling and enterprise development.

Through these partnerships, the Ministry has undertaken another positive step in strengthening its institutional capacity for quality assessment, independent monitoring, data-driven decision-making, innovation, entrepreneurship and enterprise development, while building enabling ecosystems that support sustainable economic opportunities for minority communities.

*****

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported suicide of a woman gang-raped in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh
Issues notices to the District Magistrate and Senior Superintendent of Police, Jhansi, for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a 19 year-old woman committed suicide after being gang-raped by six people, including three minors. Reportedly, the woman went to a cattle barn for some work when the six accused allegedly caught her and gang-raped her.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Senior Superintendent of Police and the District Magistrate, Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the next of kin of the deceased.

According to the media report, carried on 23rd September 2026, the victim was distressed by the threats to circulate the video and consumed poison.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India’s Online Short-Term Internship Programme for September 2026 concludes, 95 university-level students from diverse academic backgrounds, shortlisted out of 1008 applicants, completed the programme
Chairing the valedictory session, NHRC Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi encourages interns to practise and share human rights values in everyday conduct
Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani calls upon interns to make human rights a way of life
Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal urges interns to become torch bearers of human rights
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme (OSTI) of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India concluded today with 95 university-level students completing it. The internship began on 14th September 2026. The interns were shortlisted out of 1008 applicants from 19 states and union territories across the country.

Chairing the valedictory session, NHRC Member, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi, congratulated the interns on successful completion of the programme. He emphasised that the two-week training programme was not merely a journey but a valuable learning experience. Urging the interns to ensure that their efforts do not go in vain, he highlighted the importance of “Preach, Practice and Perform”, stressing that learning about human rights should continue throughout life and that the knowledge gained must be practised and shared with others.

Calling upon the interns to demonstrate human rights values in their everyday conduct, Justice Sarangi urged them to be compassionate towards others, including senior citizens and persons with disabilities and to extend appropriate consideration to their needs. He said that as young people, the interns carried great expectations for the development of the country and society.

Addressing the interns, NHRC Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani said that the conclusion of the internship marked not an end but the beginning of a new responsibility. She urged them to carry forward a commitment to human rights, the Constitution and the nation, stressing that human rights are about dignity, justice, compassion and responsibility towards one another and should become a way of life.

Emphasising that human rights and patriotism complement each other, Smt. Sayani urged the interns to respect the Constitution, protect human dignity, serve the vulnerable and stand for justice. Drawing on Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam and Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah, she called upon them to become human rights ambassadors in their communities and highlighted “knowledge, compassion and service” as guiding principles for contributing to a stronger, more just and humane India.

In his address, NHRC Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal, congratulated the interns and emphasised the importance of developing sensitivity towards human dignity in everyday life. He said that academic learning is meaningful when translated into practice. Highlighting the value of teamwork and communication skills, he said that the team activities helped inculcate team spirit and collaborative skills. He urged the interns to become torch bearers of human rights by creating greater awareness of its practical dimensions in society.

Before this, NHRC Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar, presented an overview of the internship programme, highlighting the opportunity provided to the interns to interact with NHRC Members, senior NHRC officers, eminent experts, academicians, Core Group members and representatives of civil society organisations. He expressed hope that the programme enriched the interns’ understanding of human rights. He also announced the winners of competitions, including book review, group research project presentation and declamation. Smt. Monika Joon delivered the vote of thanks.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles Undertakes Cleanliness Drives and Awareness Initiatives Across Organisations under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign, Divisional Heads inspected their respective Sections on 24 September 2026 at GPOA-3, Netaji Nagar, New Delhi, with a view to reviewing the prevailing standards of cleanliness, hygiene and general upkeep of the workplace. During the inspections, emphasis was laid on maintaining clean and orderly workspaces, ensuring proper disposal of waste, removing unwanted and obsolete materials, and promoting a clean, hygienic and conducive working environment. The exercise also aimed to sensitise officials towards the importance of cleanliness and to reinforce their collective responsibility for sustaining the principles of Swachhata in day-to-day office functioning.

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026,” the Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) undertook various cleanliness and awareness initiatives under the themes of “Clean Public Places,” “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy,” and “Swachh Paathshala .

As part of these initiatives, cleanliness drives, awareness programmes, and various community engagement activities were organized at multiple locations across different areas, with the active participation of JCI officials and employees, as well as members of the public.

These activities were aimed at promoting cleanliness, hygiene, civic responsibility, environmental awareness, and active public participation in creating and maintaining clean, hygienic, and sustainable surroundings. Through these collective efforts, JCI reinforced its commitment to fostering a culture of cleanliness and encouraging greater community involvement in the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign.

Cleanliness activities in Public Places:

  • Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI), Kharupetia Departmental Purchase Centre (DPC), Darrang District, under the Guwahati Regional Office, Assam, in association with Govt. Model Women’s College, Mangaldai, Assam, organized cleanliness activities and installed dustbins at public places to promote awareness about cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene, waste management, and environmental responsibility.

  • Samsi, Departmental Purchase Centre (DPC), Malda Region, conducted a cleanliness drive in the market area in front of the SBI ATM, with the objective of promoting cleanliness, hygiene, proper waste management, and environmental responsibility among the public.

  • Lakhipur Departmental Purchase Centre (DPC), Golapara district, Assam, under Guwahati Regional Office, conducted a cleanliness drive at Kharubucha Point Bus Stop. The activity focused on cleaning the public area and promoting awareness about cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene, and responsible waste management among the local community and commuters.

 

 

 

  • A cleanliness drive was conducted at Abhayapuri Rajbari Main Road, Abhayapuri, Bongaigaon District, Assam, under the Gauripur Region. The activity focused on maintaining cleanliness in the public area and promoting awareness about sanitation, hygiene, proper waste management, and environmental responsibility among the local community.

Jan Bhagidari Advocacy

  • The Jute Corporation of India organized various sports activities at different locations across India under the “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy” initiative. The activities encouraged active participation, teamwork, fitness, and awareness among employees and members of the public, fostering a spirit of community participation and collective responsibility.

 

National Jute Board (NJB)

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign, Employees of the National Jute Board (NJB) undertook a cleanliness drive at the Jute Diversified Product (JDP) units, with the objective of promoting cleanliness, hygiene and proper waste-management practices in the jute sector.

The cleanliness drive was conducted at Recrust International and SL Packaging, wherein the employees/workers of the respective units actively participated along with the Employees of the National Jute Board in cleaning.

During the visit, the premises of the units were inspected and cleanliness and waste-management practices were reviewed. It was encouraging to observe that the premises were already being maintained in a clean and hygienic condition, reflecting the commitment of the workers and management towards maintaining a healthy and sustainable working environment. The existing practices demonstrated awareness among the workers regarding cleanliness, proper handling of waste and maintenance of the workplace.

The National Jute Board appreciated the efforts of the management and workers of the participating JDP units in maintaining high standards of cleanliness. The activity reinforced the message that cleanliness is a continuous collective responsibility and encouraged all stakeholders to sustain these practices as part of the objectives of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign.

The cleanliness drive concluded with a positive appreciation of the efforts undertaken by the participating units towards maintaining a clean, hygienic and environmentally responsible workplace.

 

THE COTTON CORPORATION OF INDIA LTD.

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, a Clean Desk and Clean Campus activity was conducted at the Head Office and Branch Offices with active participation from all employees. Employees cleaned and organized their workspaces, cupboards, and surrounding areas, while unwanted materials were identified and segregated.

Under the “Kabad Se Jugaad” initiative, scrap and unusable materials were segregated for systematic disposal, promoting the 3R principles – Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, while also exploring the potential for revenue generation through recyclable scrap.

The initiative strengthened awareness among employees about cleanliness and encouraged collective responsibility towards maintaining a clean, organized, and hygienic workplace.

 

 

National Handloom Development Corporation Limited (NHDC)

राष्‍ट्रीय हथकरघा विकास निगम लिमिटेड, नोएडा -  दिनांक 24 सितम्‍बर 2026 को अपराह्न 2.30 बजे, स्‍वच्‍छता नोडल अधिकारी द्वारा स्‍वच्‍छता व्यवस्था का औचक निरीक्षण किया गया। निरीक्षण के दौरान कार्यालय/परिसर में साफ-सफाई, कूड़ा निस्तारण, शौचालयों की स्वच्छता तथा आसपास के क्षेत्र की स्थिति का जायजा लिया गया। नोडल अधिकारी ने संबंधित कर्मचारियों को स्वच्छता व्यवस्था नियमित रूप से बनाए रखने, कूड़े का उचित निस्तारण करने तथा किसी भी प्रकार की गंदगी न होने देने के निर्देश दिए। उन्होंने कहा कि स्वच्छ एवं स्वस्थ वातावरण बनाए रखना सभी की सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी है और इसमें किसी भी प्रकार की लापरवाही स्वीकार नहीं की जाएगी।

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Recovery to Renewed Purpose
Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts in Hailakandi Assam Support Helps Sandeep Rebuild Family Ties and Return to Work
Now Employed at the Centre That Supported His Recovery
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

Sandeep (name changed), 33, grew up in a supportive family in Assam. After studying through Class 9, he moved to Guwahati to stay with his aunt and seek work. He learned to drive and began earning a living, but substance use, which began under peer influence, gradually developed into dependency.

His health, work and relationships suffered. Much of his income went towards substance use, leaving him under financial strain and increasingly isolated. Sandeep wanted to recover, regain his family’s trust and become financially independent. His family continued to encourage him to seek help.

On 6 September 2025, Sandeep received support through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) run by South Borbond Gram Unnayan Samity in Hailakandi.

The centre provided medical care, psychological and family counselling, rehabilitation support, and motivational and behavioural guidance. Group activities and life-skills guidance helped him build healthier routines, manage stress and reconnect with others.

Sandeep while expressing his emotions and happiness said, “With my family's support and the care I received at IRCA, I am rebuilding my life and working again”.

Following his treatment, Sandeep has made positive progress in his recovery. He is working to maintain a life free from substance use and has reconnected with his family. He now works as a multi-tasking staff member at IRCA Hailakandi, giving him greater financial stability and a chance to contribute to the centre that supported his recovery.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates fourth edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show in Greater Noida
Modi Ji has made political stability his hallmark, by winning people’s trust as Prime Minister for three consecutive terms, he has implemented policies on the ground
By making changes in policies based on experience, formulating new policies, and demonstrating clarity in all of them, Modi Ji has made India an attractive manufacturing hub for the entire world
Amidst so much upheaval and unrest around the world, and despite numerous obstacles, India’s growth rate is rising today
Those who see India as a ‘dead economy’ have, in fact, a dead mindset themselves — that is why they cannot see India’s vibrancy and growth
Due to the double-engine government, UP is today becoming fear-free, a centre of investment, and the engine of the country’s development
For a favourable investment climate — good law and order, a conducive industrial policy, a proactive government, and the enthusiasm to facilitate — all four of these are present in UP
This trade fair will make it easier for producers across UP to expand their trade and production, and will help take UP’s identity to the world
The same UP, whose law-and-order situation forced the investment summit to be held in Delhi in 2013, is today setting a target of a $1 trillion economy — this is the magic of the double-engine government
Where earlier a cottage industry of vehicle theft and chain-snatching used to thrive, today defence corridors, vehicle manufacturing, and medical device parks are coming up
BrahMos missiles manufactured in UP keep Pakistan on edge, while the AK-203 assault rifles manufactured in Amethi have already struck fear into the hearts of Naxalites and terrorists
‘One District, One Product’ initiative has brought about significant progress for the youth, small entrepreneurs, and small-scale industries, and has emerged as a key driver of State’s economic development
Paying tribute to Pt.  Deendayal Upadhyaya Ji on his 110th birth anniversary, Union Home Minister said that
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the fourth edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show (UPITS) in Greater Noida. On this occasion, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath and many other dignitaries were present.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today is a very important day. He said that 12 years ago, on 25 September itself, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had announced the ‘Make in India’ mission. Today’s programme is one that paves the way for ‘Make in India’. Over the past 12 years, the Central Government and the State Governments together have walked the path of ‘Make in India’ and worked to make India a global hub of production, design and innovation. Shri Shah said that 12 years ago the Indian economy was counted among the Fragile 5, and today the Indian economy is among the Top 5, which is the result of Prime Minister Modi’s ‘Make in India’ policy.

Shri Amit Shah said that 25th September is the 110th birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya ji. He said that for the first time after independence Deendayal Upadhyaya ji placed before the country a free trade and free agriculture-based economic policy. The same economic policy later became the foundation of India’s development, first under Atal ji and thereafter under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi. Deendayal ji also laid the foundation of organisation-based politics.

Union Home Minister said that a fear-free Uttar Pradesh is emerging as an investment hub and the engine of India’s development today. This transformation has taken place because of the double-engine government. Due to this change, we can set the target of making Uttar Pradesh’s economy a 1-trillion-dollar economy. He said that buyers from across the world are present at trade fair today, and this will certainly lead to a massive increase in investment, production and sales in Uttar Pradesh. This is the fourth edition of the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Fair. In the first edition, the world was introduced to the transformation that had taken place in Uttar Pradesh. In the second edition, an intent to invest in Uttar Pradesh was expressed. In the third edition, investors came to Uttar Pradesh, and today, in the fourth edition of the trade fair, they will work as partners in the state’s development towards building a 1-trillion-dollar economy. He said that the year 2025 was a year of impact, in which more than 5 lakh people visited the trade fair, more than 2,400 MoUs were signed, investment worth thousands of crores of rupees came in, and trade agreements were also concluded. Shri Shah expressed confidence that the fourth edition of the trade fair being organised in 2026 will succeed in breaking all the records of 2025.

Shri Amit Shah said that with a population of nearly 24 crore, Uttar Pradesh is the largest state in the country. It has abundant water resources, land, hardworking artisans, and now a favourable environment for industry as well. There was a time when the mafia ruled Uttar Pradesh, but in 2017 our party formed the government here and Shri Yogi Adityanath became the Chief Minister of the state. The Yogi government has eliminated the mafia across Uttar Pradesh, and it is because of this that an investment-friendly climate has been created in the state today. He said that the first conditions for an investment climate are good law & order, a favourable industrial policy, a proactive government, and the enthusiasm to facilitate industry. All four of these are present in Uttar Pradesh today, which is why an atmosphere for investment has been created here. Prime Minister Modi has made political stability his hallmark. By winning the people’s trust for three consecutive terms as Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has not only formulated policies but has also implemented them continuously on the ground. Along with putting policies into practice, Prime Minister Modi has refined them on the basis of experience and framed new policies, thereby making India an attractive manufacturing hub for the entire world.

Union Home Minister said that some people even try to dispute India’s GDP figures. Moody’s has raised India’s growth forecast from 6% to 7%. Japan’s leading rating agency Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) has upgraded India’s sovereign rating from BBB+ to A-. In the last quarter, India maintained its record by achieving a growth rate of 7.8%. Today, among the world’s major economies, India’s is the fastest-growing. He said that amid so much upheaval and unrest around the world, and despite numerous obstacles, India has not only sustained its growth rate but has also accelerated it further. Shri Shah said that we will fulfil the resolve given by Prime Minister Modi to the people of the country to build a ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047.

Shri Amit Shah said that our electronic exports have increased 11 times compared to 2015. In July, GST collection stood at ₹2.11 lakh crore, which is the highest collection for the month of July so far. There are 12 semiconductor projects in 6 states with an investment of more than ₹1.64 lakh crore, and our capital expenditure has broken records by crossing ₹12.2 lakh crore. All these achievements are a testament to the foundation of India’s development. He said that some people find the Indian economy a “dead economy,” but those whose thinking itself is dead cannot see its vibrancy. Shri Shah said that some people cannot see India’s development. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, we have signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with Mauritius, UAE, Austria, the organisation of four European countries, UK, Oman, New Zealand, and European Union. These FTAs have multiplied the export potential of our industries many times over. Shri Shah said that despite various adversities, the Indian economy has sustained its growth rate.

Union Home Minister said that today investment is flowing into defence manufacturing at the six nodes of the Defence Corridor in Jhansi, Chitrakoot, Lucknow, Agra, Aligarh and Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh. As a result, not only Uttar Pradesh but defence products across the country have developed, and our defence production stands at ₹1,78,000 crore. Compared to 2013-14, we have increased the export of defence products by 56 times, and today Indian defence products are being exported to 80 countries. He said that Uttar Pradesh has made a very significant contribution to this. The Yogi government has not only established the Defence Corridor but has also done extensive work to facilitate it, link it with infrastructure and create favourable policies. The BrahMos missiles manufactured in UP keep Pakistan on edge, while the AK-203 assault rifles manufactured in Amethi have already struck fear into the hearts of Naxalites and terrorists.

Shri Amit Shah said that during the tenure of previous governments, a crime industry was thriving in Uttar Pradesh, and the state had become a hub for the manufacture of country-made pistols and illegal firearms. Vehicle theft operated like a cottage industry in the cities of the state, and chain-snatching even provided an opportunity for the youth to show off their skills. Today, after 10 years, the country-made pistols industry has been replaced by a Defence Corridor, vehicle theft by vehicle manufacturing, and the chain-snatching industry by Medical Device Parks. He said that today Uttar Pradesh has become a major destination for attracting investment, and this transformation has taken place due to the double-engine government. He said that the very Uttar Pradesh - whose law & order situation had necessitated holding the 2013 investment summit in Delhi - is today setting a target of becoming a $1 trillion economy; this is the magic of the 'double-engine' government.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that after the formation of the Yogi government, the complete goondaism of the previous governments’ tenure has been wiped out, and this has created a favourable environment for setting up industries here. Uttar Pradesh has achieved good results through its lucrative industrial policy, prompt resolution of industries’ problems, and by rolling out the red carpet to attract industries from across the country to the state. Through this, the government of Yogi Adityanath has created employment opportunities for crores of youth in the state.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Noida Airport, expressways and various infrastructure projects have created a conducive environment for investment in the state. As a result, today Uttar Pradesh is progressing at a rapid pace. The metro is currently operational in seven cities of Uttar Pradesh, which is the highest in any state in the country. We have launched the ‘One District, One Product’ (ODOP) scheme here. Due to the nurturing of traditional crafts and industries along with the ODOP initiative, there has been a significant rise among the youth, small entrepreneurs and small-scale industries of the state, which has become the pivot of Uttar Pradesh’s economic development.

Union Home Minister said that there was a time when people from Uttar Pradesh used to migrate to other states of the country in search of employment, and today the youth of the same Uttar Pradesh are getting employment in their own state due to the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme. Whether it is the carpets of Bhadohi, the brassware of Moradabad, the glass of Firozabad, the woodcraft of Saharanpur, the perfume of Kannauj or the silk sarees of Banaras — all these have carved a distinct identity across the country. Just now, the website of ‘One District, One Cuisine’ (ODOC) was also launched here, through which Varanasi’s Malaiyo and Tiranga Barfi, Agra’s Petha, Mathura’s Peda and Meerut’s Gajak will be made available to the people of the entire country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya. Shri Shah said that this trade fair will greatly facilitate the trade and production of producers across Uttar Pradesh and help in establishing UP’s identity worldwide.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Operation Drishti: AFMS conducts 220 sight-restoring surgeries during 2-day Mega Eye Surgical Camp at Tangdhar along LoC
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

          Surgeons of the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) carried out 220 sight-restoring surgeries during the 10th edition of first-of-its-kind Mega Eye Surgical Camp, held under Operation Drishti, at an underground operation theatre in Tangdhar in Kupwara, a shelling prone zone, in Jammu & Kashmir along the Line of Control on September 24 & 25, 2026. Most interventions were cataract surgeries, along with selective retinal procedures and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery.

          Over the two days, the camp was visited by Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth who interacted with patients and distributed medicines & gifts. DG AFMS Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja also visited the camp and appreciated the surgeons and the local team for their exceptional skills & efforts.

          The camp was led by Head of Ophthalmology at Army Hospital (Research & Referral), Delhi Cantonment Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, whose team carried advanced phacoemulsification, vitreoretinal and glaucoma equipment across mountainous terrain. Patients from Khawarpora, Tangdar, Tadd, Bagbela, Yangdar and neighbouring hamlets came after screening and a broadcast on Radio Rooh-e-Karnah, with the Indian Army guiding each one from arrival to recovery.

AFMS’ series of mega surgical eye camps envisaged by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh have, so far, screened over 1.50 lakh patients. Over 3,500 surgeries have been conducted across 10 cities. The 11th camp in this series will be held in Srinagar from September 27 to 29, 2026. The formal closing ceremony will be graced by Lieutenant Governor of Jammu & Kashmir, Shri Manoj Sinha on September 30, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
DARPG releases the 49th Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for States/UTs for August, 2026
A total of 98,997 PG cases received for the States/UTs and 79,639 PG cases redressed in August, 2026
Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years, 1,270 training courses have been completed, in which ~42,011 officers have been trained
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) released the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) 49th monthly report for States/UTs for August, 2026. The said report provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal by the States/UTs.

In August, 2026, 98,997 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 79,639 PG cases were redressed. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in August, 2026 with 28,939 PG cases, followed by Gujarat with 6,810 PG cases. As of 31st August, 2026, the total pendency of PG cases on the CPGRAMS portal stands at 2,53,040 across all States and UTs. Moreover, 23 States/UTs have more than 1,000 pending PG cases each.

The report provides the data for new users registered on CPGRAMS through CPGRAMS Portal during August, 2026. A total of 1,38,801 new users have registered on CPGRAMS in August, 2026, through various channels, out of which, 42,054 registrations are from West Bengal.

The report also provides the state-wise analysis on the grievances registered through Common Service Centres in August, 2026. CPGRAMS has been integrated with the Common Service Centre (CSC) portal and is available at more than 5 lakh CSCs, associating with 2.5 lakh Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). A total of 8,999 grievances have been registered through the Common Service Centres in the month of August, 2026.

The report also provides the total number of training programmes conducted and officers trained over the last five financial years under the Sevottam Scheme. Between FY 2022–23 and FY 2026–27, a total of 1,217 training courses were conducted, training ~40,077 officers.

Key Highlights for the month of August, 2026, are as follows:

General Highlights

  • Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27), 1,270 training courses have been completed, in which ~42,011 officers have been trained.
  • In August 2026, West Bengal received the highest number of grievances through CSCs, constituting 44% of the total 8,999 grievances received via CSCs.

Status of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • In August, 2026, 98,997 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 79,639 PG cases were redressed.
  • Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in August, 2026 with 28,939 PG cases, followed by Gujarat and Rajasthan with 6,810 and 5,895 PG cases respectively.

Status of Pendency of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Women Power Takes Centre Stage at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 as 14 Young Women Represent Team India Across Diverse Skills
From Chemical Laboratory Technology and Logistics to Visual Merchandising, Hospitality, Beauty and Bakery, women competitors showcase India’s expanding skills landscape
Women make up more than one-fifth of Team India’s 70-member competitor contingent at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi

India’s growing participation of women across diverse vocational and technical skills is finding expression on the global stage at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, with 14 young women representing Team India across a wide spectrum of skill categories.

The women competitors are part of India’s 70-member contingent competing across 63 skills at the 48th WorldSkills Competition being held in Shanghai from 22–27 September 2026.

Significantly, women competitors are representing India across a broad mix of technical, specialised, creative and service-oriented skills. These include Chemical Laboratory Technology, Logistics and Freight Forwarding, Visual Merchandising, Fashion Technology, Retail Sales and Health and Social Care, alongside Hotel Reception, Restaurant Service, Cooking, Painting and Decorating, Hairdressing, Beauty Therapy, Bakery and Patisserie and Confectionery.

The breadth of this participation reflects the widening occupational choices available to young women and their growing presence across skills that extend well beyond traditional career pathways.

Ms. Manisha Sensarma, Official Delegate, WorldSkills India and Senior Economic Adviser, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said, “The participation of these young women at WorldSkills Shanghai reflects an encouraging shift in India’s skilling landscape. What is particularly significant is the diversity of skills in which they are competing from chemical laboratory technology, logistics and visual merchandising to hospitality, beauty and specialised crafts. It reinforces a simple but powerful message that skills have no gender. Our effort is to ensure that young women have the opportunity, training and confidence to choose careers based on their aptitude and aspirations, and to compete at the highest global standards.”

The participants include Sampada Desai in Chemical Laboratory Technology; Mehrunissa Begum in Logistics and Freight Forwarding; Anuja Ajay Vare in Visual Merchandising; Vidhi Niravkumar Suthar in Fashion Technology; Saniya Joshi in Retail Sales; Vishnupriya Sunil in Health and Social Care; Rashmeet Kaur Hanspal in Hotel Reception; Jhansirani Rout in Restaurant Service; Thanushree Magesh in Cooking; Muskan in Painting and Decorating; Jui Santosh Sapke in Hairdressing; T. Sabir Sutar in Beauty Therapy; Smriti Nambiar in Bakery; and Krishnanjali Sahoo in Patisserie and Confectionery.

Their participation reflects the widening horizons of India’s skilling ecosystem, with young women increasingly exploring careers across technical, creative, healthcare, logistics, hospitality and service sectors.

WorldSkills provides competitors an opportunity to benchmark their capabilities against international standards and learn alongside some of the finest young skilled professionals from around the world. Team India’s women competitors have undergone intensive preparation and training ahead of the global competition, sharpening their technical capabilities and their ability to perform under exacting international standards.

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship continues to encourage greater participation of women in vocational education, apprenticeships and industry-linked training, while supporting wider occupational choices and pathways to sustainable livelihoods.

As competitions progress in Shanghai, these young women represent a generation increasingly confident about building careers through skills, technology, craftsmanship and professional excellence.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Media Registration Opens for India Mining Week 2026
Journalists and Media Professionals Invited to Register for Coverage of India’s Flagship Mining and Minerals Platform
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Media Registration for India Mining Week (IMW) 2026 is now open for journalists, media professionals and content creators wishing to cover the three-day international event, scheduled to be held from 15 to 17 November 2026 at Yashobhoomi Convention Centre, New Delhi.

The three-day summit will be organised under the theme “Stronger Resources, Smarter Mining, Sustainable Tomorrow”, reflecting India’s vision of building a technologically advanced, globally competitive and environmentally responsible mining sector.  The event will bring together policymakers, government representatives, mining and mineral companies, investors, technology innovators, equipment manufacturers, researchers and international stakeholders to deliberate on developments across the mining and minerals sector.

The summit will feature a high-level conference, international exhibition, technical sessions, leadership dialogues and dedicated networking opportunities. Discussions will focus on critical themes including mineral security, exploration, digitisation, automation, mine safety, sustainability, critical minerals, resource efficiency, innovation and the future of mining in an evolving global landscape. The event is expected to provide a platform for discussions on the future of India’s mining ecosystem and the evolving global mineral landscape.

Media registration is open through the official India Mining Week website- https://www.indiaminingweek.org/media-registration/

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
AIIA and 132 ECO Task Force Join Hands for Ashwagandha Plantation and Research in Aravalli Landscape
10,000 Ashwagandha Saplings to be Scientifically Monitored at Terriers Herbal Garden, Bhatti Mines
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, and 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT have launched the Ashwagandha Plantation and Research Initiative at the Terriers Herbal Garden, Bhatti Mines, South Delhi. The initiative brings together Ayurveda, medicinal plant research, biodiversity conservation and environmental restoration.

The programme was held on September 24, 2026, under the leadership of Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director, AIIA, and Colonel Mohan Singh, Commanding Officer, 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT.

Under the collaborative initiative, 10,000 Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera (L.) Dunal) saplings will be planted and subjected to scientific monitoring. The initiative combines AIIA’s expertise in Ayurveda, medicinal plants and scientific research with the Ecological Battalion’s experience in plantation, biodiversity conservation and environmental restoration.

The Ashwagandha plants will be regularly monitored, observed and documented to generate information on their growth and adaptation under the local climatic and environmental conditions of the Aravalli landscape. The initiative will also provide an opportunity to link traditional Ayurvedic knowledge on medicinal plants with scientific research.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said, “This initiative brings together the rich Ayurvedic knowledge of medicinal plants with scientific research and ecological restoration. Ashwagandha is an important medicinal plant of Ayurveda, and its systematic cultivation, conservation and scientific documentation can contribute to both knowledge generation and biodiversity conservation. Such collaborations reflect our commitment to taking Ayurveda beyond clinical practice and strengthening its connection with nature and sustainability.”

The programme brought together Dr. Meena Deogade, Head, Department of Dravyaguna, AIIA, faculty members Dr. Shivani Ghildiyal, Associate Professor, and Dr. Bidhan Mahajon, Assistant Professor, along with PhD Research Scholars of the Department and officers and personnel of 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT.

The planning and implementation of the plantation initiative between the two organisations was coordinated by Major Jai Singh Shekhawat of 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT and Major (Dr.) Ashish Kumar of AIIA.

The initiative at Bhatti Mines has environmental significance as the area forms part of Delhi’s Southern Ridge and the Aravalli landscape. The 132 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) ECO RAJPUT has been engaged in plantation and restoration activities in areas affected and degraded by mining.

The Terriers Herbal Garden already houses around 200 species of medicinal and Ayurvedic significance, which have been planted and conserved. These include Parijata (Harshringar), Amla (Indian Gooseberry) and Ghritkumari (Aloe Vera). AIIA has been entrusted with providing technical support for the proper maintenance, scientific management and guidance of the herbal garden.

Ashwagandha is regarded in Ayurveda as an important medicinal plant for promoting health. The National Medicinal Plants Board, Ministry of Ayush, has also undertaken the “Ashwagandha – A Health Promoter” campaign to raise awareness about its health-related importance.

The initiative seeks to link scientific research on medicinal plants with environmental restoration at Bhatti Mines, supporting biodiversity conservation and the development of an eco-friendly ecosystem.

The initiative carries the message: “Roots in Ayurveda – Conserve Biodiversity – Restore Ecosystems.” It seeks to connect India’s traditional medicinal-plant knowledge with scientific research, biodiversity conservation and efforts to restore the green landscape of the Aravallis.

item.title: Technological Sovereignty Crucial to National Sovereignty, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh at CSIR@85 Foundation Day
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Technological Sovereignty Crucial to National Sovereignty, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh at CSIR@85 Foundation Day CSIR Among Few Institutions That Have Led India’s Post-Independence Journey; Its Laboratories Have Given Distinct Identity to States Through Their Success Stories: Dr. Jitendra Singh Industry Must Become a Co-Creator, Not Merely a Partner, in Technology Development, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh CSIR Must Shorten the Journey from Discovery to Deployment and Develop Globally Competitive Indigenous Technologies: Dr. Jitendra Singh Dr. Jitendra…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Technological Sovereignty Crucial to National Sovereignty, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh at CSIR@85 Foundation Day
CSIR Among Few Institutions That Have Led India’s Post-Independence Journey; Its Laboratories Have Given Distinct Identity to States Through Their Success Stories: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Industry Must Become a Co-Creator, Not Merely a Partner, in Technology Development, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh
CSIR Must Shorten the Journey from Discovery to Deployment and Develop Globally Competitive Indigenous Technologies: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Unveils CSIR Mascot; Releases CSIR@85 Postal Stamp, Industry Connect Video and Technology Compendium
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi

Technological sovereignty is crucial to national sovereignty and India cannot remain dependent indefinitely on imported technologies in areas critical to its economy, security and development, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said today.

Addressing the 85th Foundation Day celebrations of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) at C. R. Subramaniam Hall, NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi, he said CSIR laboratories must identify areas of critical technological dependence and work towards indigenous solutions that are globally competitive in performance, quality and cost. India’s ambition, he said, must go beyond import substitution and extend to becoming a technology provider to the world.

The 85th Foundation Day celebrations were attended by Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, CSIR, Directors of CSIR laboratories, senior scientists, researchers, officials, industry representatives, startups and other stakeholders. More than 40 ambassadors from 14 countries were also present and joined the visit to the CSIR exhibits.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said CSIR is among the few institutions that have led India’s journey after Independence, having begun its own journey in 1942, before the country became independent. He said the organisation represents a rich scientific legacy built over more than eight decades and has developed capabilities across a wide range of domains. The Minister said the challenge before CSIR is to live up to this legacy by continuously renewing its scientific and technological work according to the current and futuristic requirements of the country.

Referring to the diverse achievements of CSIR laboratories, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the organisation’s success stories have increasingly become associated with the identity of different States and regions. He cited examples of CSIR’s contributions in areas ranging from leather technologies and jewellery to healthcare, agriculture, road technologies, food technology and aerospace. He said it is a matter of satisfaction that different regions can increasingly associate themselves with specific scientific and technological achievements emerging from CSIR laboratories.

The Minister said a significant change in the last decade has been the increased visibility of scientific achievements and their greater connection with citizens. He said the scientific work existed earlier as well, but its success stories are now reaching people in a more visible and direct manner. Referring to the opening up of scientific institutions and facilities to wider public participation, he said that if scientific work and services are intended to bring ease of living to citizens, citizens should also know what is being developed and how they can benefit from it.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said CSIR must shorten the journey from laboratory to industry and from discovery to deployment, with stronger industry linkage from the very beginning of a project. He said the traditional approach of developing a technology in the laboratory and subsequently looking for an industry partner needs to give way to a model in which industry is involved from the stage of defining the problem itself.

“Industry should be a co-creator, not only a partner,” Dr. Jitendra Singh said, explaining that scientists understand the science and technological possibilities, while industry understands the market, scale, cost and customer requirements. Bringing these capabilities together from the beginning, he said, can significantly improve the prospects of successful technology translation.

He called for deeper and sustained relationships between CSIR laboratories and industries relevant to their respective domains and encouraged large companies, MSMEs and startups to regard CSIR laboratories as R&D partners. He said industry should be involved in technology development in a manner that takes into account market requirements and the ability to scale and sustain a technology. He also said that while starting a startup may be relatively easy, sustaining one requires stronger linkages between technology, industry and the market.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said technological sovereignty has become increasingly important in a rapidly changing global environment. He said India cannot achieve national sovereignty without technological sovereignty and needs to reduce dependence on external sources in critical areas. He referred to the country’s efforts in nuclear energy, clean energy and other emerging areas, and said the coming years would increasingly test India’s ability to develop and control critical technologies.

The Minister also referred to the National Quantum Mission, IndiaAI Mission and India Genome Mission, saying that India has moved towards a cross-generational and cross-ministerial approach in science and technology. He said this approach is not confined to individual departments but reflects a wider whole-of-government and whole-of-nation effort to address emerging technological challenges.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said CSIR must remain an all-time relevant scientific organisation by continuously rejuvenating its research priorities instead of repeatedly relying on past accomplishments. Referring to newer technologies and applications emerging from CSIR laboratories, he mentioned electric tractors, indigenous pharmaceutical technologies, food technologies, continuous-flow processes, advanced road technologies, solar technologies and mechanised sewer-cleaning solutions. He said CSIR’s focus should remain on present and futuristic national requirements.

The Minister also stressed the importance of making scientific institutions more accessible to society. Recalling his interactions with farmers and other stakeholders, he said greater public engagement helps citizens understand the work taking place inside scientific laboratories. He said CSIR’s technologies and scientific capabilities must ultimately translate into benefits for citizens, industry and the wider economy.

During the Foundation Day celebrations, Dr. Jitendra Singh unveiled CIRA: CSIR’s Innovation and Research Ambassador, the new CSIR mascot. He also released the CSIR@85 special postal stamp, CSIR Industry Connect Video and CSIR Technology Compendium. The programme also featured the CSIR-Industry Technology Exhibition, technology transfers and the CSIR Sci-Art Gallery, bringing together scientific achievements, technology development, industry engagement and public outreach.

Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, in her welcome address, described CSIR@85 as a historically important, scientifically significant and strategically important milestone. She spoke about CSIR’s network of 37 laboratories and more than 10,000 personnel, and its work across diverse scientific and technological domains. She also acknowledged the contribution of the extended CSIR family comprising scientists, researchers, technical personnel, industry, MSMEs, startups and other partners.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the achievements of CSIR ultimately represent the collective contribution of generations of scientists, engineers, researchers, technical personnel, administrative colleagues and support staff. Congratulating the entire CSIR family on completing 85 years, he said the organisation must now prepare itself for the scientific and technological requirements of the coming decades.

As India works towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, Dr. Jitendra Singh said CSIR has a distinctive responsibility because its own journey began before Independence. While India is preparing long-term roadmaps for 2030 and 2047, he said CSIR must aspire to carry its legacy forward beyond 2047.

“When India reaches 2047, I wish CSIR would have lived up to its legacy and travelled and progressed beyond 2047,” the Minister said.

He said the next phase of CSIR’s journey must be defined by faster translation of research into technology, stronger industry partnerships, greater technological self-reliance and continued relevance to India’s emerging national requirements. With its scientific strength spread across 37 laboratories, CSIR, he said, has the institutional capacity to contribute to the technologies that will shape India’s journey towards 2047 and beyond.

*****

NKR/AK

item.title: Wellness Is Not Mere Absence of Disease; Focus Must Shift to Preventive Healthcare and Physical and Mental Well-Being: Dr. Jitendra Singh
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Wellness Is Not Mere Absence of Disease; Focus Must Shift to Preventive Healthcare and Physical and Mental Well-Being: Dr. Jitendra Singh India’s Health Approach Has Evolved Over the Last Decade with Greater Emphasis on Ayurveda, Yoga and Wellness Centres Healthy Younger Generation Will Be Critical to Realising Viksit Bharat 2047: Dr. Jitendra Singh Rising Life Expectancy Has Also Changed India’s Health Challenges, with Lifestyle Diseases Becoming More Prominent, says Dr. Jitendra Singh Science and Translational Research Can Help Take Affordable Healthcare…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Wellness Is Not Mere Absence of Disease; Focus Must Shift to Preventive Healthcare and Physical and Mental Well-Being: Dr. Jitendra Singh
India’s Health Approach Has Evolved Over the Last Decade with Greater Emphasis on Ayurveda, Yoga and Wellness Centres
Healthy Younger Generation Will Be Critical to Realising Viksit Bharat 2047: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Rising Life Expectancy Has Also Changed India’s Health Challenges, with Lifestyle Diseases Becoming More Prominent, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Science and Translational Research Can Help Take Affordable Healthcare Solutions to Larger Populations: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi

“Wellness is not mere absence of disease”; the focus now has to be on preventive healthcare and physical and mental well-being, said Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, at the Health & Wellness Summit 2026. He said that over the last decade, India has increasingly moved towards a broader understanding of health, with greater emphasis on Ayurveda, Yoga and wellness centres alongside modern healthcare. A healthy younger generation, he said, will be central to realising the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that health is no longer limited to being free from disease or receiving treatment for a particular ailment. It encompasses physical and mental well-being, the environment in which people live and work, work-life balance and overall ease of living. This changing understanding of health makes prevention and healthy living an important part of the healthcare approach.

The Minister said that India’s substantial rise in life expectancy has also brought a changing disease profile. At the time of Independence, India’s average life expectancy was barely around 45 years; today, people are living considerably longer, while health challenges such as cardiovascular diseases and Type 2 diabetes, along with other lifestyle-related non-communicable diseases, have become increasingly prominent.

He said that advances in healthcare and wider access to medical facilities have significantly improved the ability to diagnose and treat serious illnesses. The next phase of healthcare, however, must place greater emphasis on prevention, early detection and maintaining well-being, rather than relying only on treatment after disease occurs.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Government has adopted a broader approach to healthcare, combining improved access to treatment with preventive and grassroots interventions. He cited the expansion of medical education and initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat as part of efforts to make healthcare more accessible and reduce the financial burden of serious illness on families.

The Minister said that science and technology have an important role in addressing emerging health challenges, particularly by developing solutions that are affordable, accessible and suited to local needs. India’s scientific ecosystem, he said, has demonstrated its ability to respond to major public health challenges, including during COVID-19, when Indian laboratories rapidly isolated and sequenced the SARS-CoV-2 genome, contributing to the development of indigenous vaccines.

He said that the focus now must also be on translating scientific research into technologies and products that can benefit large populations. Translational research, bringing together medicine, science, technology and industry, can help develop affordable diagnostics, biosensors, drug-delivery technologies and other healthcare solutions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to the importance of early screening for inherited disorders, particularly among newborns and pregnant women. Programmes such as UMMID (Unique Methods of Management and Treatment of Inherited Disorders) are helping strengthen early detection and management, demonstrating how scientific capabilities can be deployed for preventive healthcare.

He said that India’s health priorities must evolve alongside the country’s changing demographic and disease profile. The transition towards longer lives makes it increasingly important to ensure that people do not merely live longer, but also enjoy better physical and mental well-being.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that continued collaboration among medical practitioners, researchers, industry and other stakeholders will be important in developing practical solutions for emerging health challenges. The objective, he said, should be to build a healthier India in which preventive healthcare and wellness become an integral part of the country’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

*****

item.description: Ministry of Finance DRI seizes 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold worth around Rs. 15 crore at Mumbai airport; three arrested Gold powder ingeniously blended with food products like milk powder, oats, rice flour and cake mix Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi Continuing its sustained crackdown on gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Mumbai Zonal Unit, based on specific intelligence, intercepted three Indian passengers arriving from Dubai at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, in the early hours of 23.09.2026, with…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold worth around Rs. 15 crore at Mumbai airport; three arrested
Gold powder ingeniously blended with food products like milk powder, oats, rice flour and cake mix
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Mumbai Zonal Unit, based on specific intelligence, intercepted three Indian passengers arriving from Dubai at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, in the early hours of 23.09.2026, with operational assistance from the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU), Mumbai Airport Customs.

Detailed examination of their baggage revealed a highly sophisticated and unusual method of concealment, wherein foreign-origin gold had been converted into fine powder and meticulously mixed with packaged food products of similar colour, texture and consistency to evade detection.

The gold powder was found concealed across several apparently ordinary food packets like milk powder, oats, various flours, Nutella and coconut milk powder. In all, approximately 33.50 kg food products mixed with gold powder were recovered from the baggage of the three passengers.

Through careful segregation and assaying, 9.40 kg foreign-origin gold, valued at approximately Rs. 14.81 crore, was recovered and seized under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962. During questioning, all three passengers admitted to acting on behalf of the same organised gold-smuggling syndicate. They were accordingly arrested under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

The operation has uncovered a novel and sophisticated method of gold smuggling, wherein powdered gold was ingeniously blended with a wide variety of packaged food products to evade routine detection.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes over 125,000 kg foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts and 41,000 kg poppy seeds worth around Rs. 20.31 crore in Assam and Mizoram in a crackdown on cross-border smuggling; four arrested
This is one of the largest seizure of smuggled areca nuts in North-East Region
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on cross-border smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized 1,25,680 kg of foreign-origin areca nuts and 41,697 kg foreign-origin poppy seeds, collectively valued at approximately Rs. 20.31 crore, in two intelligence-led operations in Mizoram and Assam. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the transportation of the smuggled poppy seeds.

On 23-24.09.26, in a major intelligence led operation in Mizoram, DRI with the assistance of Customs Champhai, 14th Battalion Assam Rifles and Champhai Police, searched three godowns in and around Ruantlang village, Champhai District, located approximately 20 km from the Indo-Myanmar border. All the premises were found locked and unattended. The search of the premises resulted in the recovery of 1,25,680 kg suspected foreign-origin areca nuts valued at around Rs. 14 Crore and 25,440 kg of poppy seeds valued at Rs. 3.81 crore. Preliminary investigation indicated that the goods had been smuggled into India from Myanmar. The goods were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Earlier on 22.09.26, based on specific intelligence regarding transportation of foreign-origin poppy seeds from the Mizoram border area towards Assam, DRI officers with the assistance of 38 Battalion Assam Rifles, intercepted two trucks near Lailapur, Silchar. Detailed examination and rummaging of the vehicles resulted in the recovery of 290 HDPE bags containing 16,257 kg foreign-origin poppy seeds. The bags bore markings indicative of foreign manufacture and trade, and the consignment was not accompanied by valid import documents. The poppy seeds, valued at approximately Rs 2.43 crore, along with the two vehicles, were seized under the Customs Act, 1962. Four persons involved in the transportation were arrested.

The seizure of foreign-origin smuggled areca nuts, one of the largest seizures of the commodity in recent years in the North-Eastern region of the country, is a significant achievement in DRI’s efforts to curb cross-border smuggling.

Poppy seeds are classified as a “Restricted” item under the ITC (HS) Classification of the Foreign Trade Policy, with import permitted subject to specified conditions, including sourcing from designated countries and registration of import contracts with the Narcotics Commissioner, Gwalior.

The seizures highlight DRI’s continued focus on intercepting smuggling networks operating through the vulnerable India-Myanmar border and preventing illicit entry of restricted and foreign-origin agricultural commodities into the country.

****

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Ministry of Ayush Resolves Over 3,100 Public Grievances under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ayush has reaffirmed its commitment to citizen-centric governance, efficient administration and timely grievance redressal through the successful implementation of Special Campaign 6, conducted from November 2025 to August 2026. The campaign focused on expediting the disposal of pending references and strengthening institutional efficiency across the Ministry and its organisations.

During the campaign period, the Ministry disposed of 3,100 out of 3,134 Public Grievances, achieving a disposal rate of nearly 99 per cent. It also resolved 454 out of 461 Public Grievance Appeals, further reinforcing its focus on addressing citizen concerns in a timely and responsive manner.

The Ministry also made significant progress in the disposal of various government references. A total of 70 references from Members of Parliament, 18 Parliamentary Assurances, 14 PMO References and 3 State Government References were disposed of during the campaign.

The focused efforts under Special Campaign 6 reflect the Ministry’s continued emphasis on responsive governance, institutional accountability and efficient public service delivery. The campaign has also provided an opportunity to strengthen internal processes and ensure that pending matters are addressed with greater urgency.

Through sustained monitoring and coordinated efforts across the Ministry and its associated organisations, Special Campaign 6 has further strengthened the mechanism for timely disposal of grievances and references. The initiative underscores the Ministry of Ayush’s commitment to transparent, accountable and citizen-oriented administration.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs for Resilient Pharmaceutical Supply Chain
Posted On: 25 SEP 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Bulk Drugs is strengthening India’s domestic capabilities in manufacturing critical Key Starting Materials (KSMs), Drug Intermediates (DIs) and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), reducing import dependence and enhancing resilience across the pharmaceutical supply chain.

Five Greenfield projects that have commissioned manufacturing facilities under the Scheme demonstrate the growing scale and diversity of domestic production, covering critical ingredients for antibiotics, cardiovascular medicines and Paracetamol.

Lyfius Pharma Pvt. Ltd., a subsidiary of Aurobindo Pharma Limited, has established a large-scale Penicillin G manufacturing facility at Kakinada SEZ in Andhra Pradesh. The project with an investment of ₹2,270.05 crore, has installed capacity of 15,000 MT per annum. 

The facility has generated 2,353 direct jobs and recorded cumulative production of ₹1,191 crore. Penicillin G is a critical fermentation-based KSM used in the production of intermediates such as 6-APA, which in turn are used for manufacturing widely prescribed antibiotics including amoxicillin and ampicillin. 

With more than 90% domestic value addition, the project resulted in the restoration of domestic manufacturing of Penicillin G after a gap of about three decades and addressed a strategically concentrated vulnerability in India's antibiotic supply chain while strengthening health security, improving supply-chain resilience and reducing exposure to external supply disruptions and sharp price movements.

Kinvan Private Limited, a DPB Group company, has established a 400 MT per annum fermentation-based manufacturing facility for Clavulanic Acid (Potassium Clavulanate) at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh.

The project with an investment of ₹504.68 crore, has generated 465 direct jobs and recorded cumulative production of ₹413 crore. This is India's first fermentation-based manufacturing facility for Potassium Clavulanate.

Clavulanic Acid is a β-lactamase inhibitor that is combined with penicillin-group antibiotics such as amoxicillin to improve their effectiveness against resistant bacteria. The project represents a large-scale bio-pharmaceutical investment in a hill State, adding to Himachal Pradesh’s pharmaceutical manufacturing base and has strengthened indigenous capabilities while reducing import dependence..

Andhra Organics Limited (AOL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Virchow Laboratories Limited, has commissioned manufacturing facilities for Sulfadiazine, Telmisartan and Olmesartan at Pydibhimavaram in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh.The projects involve a combined investment of ₹151.47 crore and have generated 221 direct employment. The company has developed the manufacturing technology in-house and has established greenfield production facilities..

Domestic production of Sulfadiazine has contributed to a substantial reduction in India's import dependence, with imports having declined by about 73% compared with the FY 2019-20 baseline since the company began supplies in 2022. Telmisartan and Olmesartan are widely used APIs for medicines prescribed for hypertension, supporting the availability of essential cardiovascular medicines.

Meghmani LLP has established a 13,500 MT per annum manufacturing facility for Para Amino Phenol (PAP) at Dahej, Gujarat, with an investment of ₹60.46 crore.

PAP is a critical starting material for Paracetamol, one of the most widely used medicines for fever and pain relief. The PLI-supported facility provides large-scale domestic capacity for PAP, which was earlier largely imported.

The project has recorded cumulative production of ₹687 crore. The facility strengthens backward integration in Paracetamol manufacturing and contributes to greater security of supply for an essential medicine used extensively across the country and has also strengthened India’s position as a reliable global supplier of Paracetamol.

Centrient Pharmaceuticals India Private Limited has established a greenfield Atorvastatin API manufacturing facility in Nawanshahr, Punjab, with an installed capacity of 206 MT per annum.

The project with an investment of ₹161.13 crore, has recorded cumulative production of ₹432 crore.

Atorvastatin is a widely prescribed cardiovascular medicine used to lower cholesterol and reduce the risk of cardiovascular events. The project has enabled the development of a supply chain with more than 80% domestic value addition, reducing dependence on imported key starting materials and supporting India's capacity to meet domestic requirements while strengthening its potential as a global supplier.

The commissioning of these facilities under the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs reflects the growing capabilities of Indian manufacturers across fermentation-based and chemically synthesised pharmaceutical inputs.

From Penicillin G and Clavulanic Acid to APIs such as Atorvastatin, Telmisartan and Olmesartan, and the key Paracetamol starting material PAP, the projects are contributing to greater domestic value addition, import substitution, employment generation and supply-chain resilience. The projects also demonstrate how targeted policy support can encourage investments in strategically important pharmaceutical manufacturing segments, strengthen backward integration and build indigenous technological capabilities.
